title: Elon Musk, who has spent $446 million on US midterms, reposts 2022 prediction on Democrats: 'Now, watch their...'
text: Elon Musk's AI company is reportedly targeting 418 homes near its Mississippi data center, with buyout offers tied to waiving noise-lawsuit claims; county records show five purchases since October 9 Elon Musk has dug up a four-year-old post about the Democrats, days before the US midterm elections he has spent nearly half a billion dollars trying to shape. On Friday (October 30), the Tesla and SpaceX CEO quote-posted his May 2022 message on X, formerly Twitter, with a short caption: "Four years ago . .. And that is exactly what happened." The post crossed 7 million views in about a day. The original post is where Elon Musk first announced his break from the Democrat party he had backed for years. "In the past I voted Democrat, because they were (mostly) the kindness party," he wrote, adding that they had become "the party of division & hate" and that he would now vote Republican. He ended with a prediction: "Now, watch their dirty tricks campaign against me unfold," followed by a popcorn emoji. Elon Musk is now the biggest single-cycle political donor in modern US history Elon Musk has put at least $445.77 million into Republican-aligned political action committees and groups since last year, according to Federal Election Commission data as of October 29. That is well above the roughly $290 million he spent backing Donald Trump and Republicans in 2024. About $200 million of it came in the final two months of campaigning alone. The biggest share, $216 million, went to his own America PAC, which has targeted 43 House and Senate races. Texas has drawn the most money. Tesla and Spacex CEO Elon Musk has poured well over $200 million into the Senate contest between Republican Ken Paxton and Democrat James Talarico, including $168 million to the Senate Leadership Fund. It is now the most expensive race of the midterms. Talarico has turned that spending into a campaign issue. "This Senate seat doesn't belong to Elon Musk," he told supporters at a rally earlier this week. How Elon Musk went from 'I've done enough' to Republicans' top backer in a year The spending is a turnaround from May 2025, when Elon Musk said, "I think I've done enough" on political donations after public backlash over his role in the early months of Trump's second term. The 2022 thread has its own backstory. When former Obama speechwriter Jon Favreau replied that Musk was backing "electric vehicle-hating climate deniers", Musk shot back that the Biden administration had tried to sideline Tesla, even though the company made twice as many EVs as the rest of the US industry combined. Ahead of the midterm elections, billionaire Elon Musk warned that a Democratic sweep of the White House and Congress in 2028 could spell the "end of democracy," outlining three moves he fears the party would make to cement its political power. Elon Musk outlines his three biggest fears from Democrats coming to power Musk outlined his three "biggest" concerns about Democrats gaining unified control of Washington, in an X post, warning that the party would move to grant statehood to Washington, DC, and Puerto Rico, legalize immigrants living in the country illegally and expand the Supreme Court. "My biggest concern is that if there is a clean sweep by Democrats of the House, Senate and Presidency in 2028, they will: 1. Make DC and Puerto Rico states to gain a strong majority in the Senate. 2. Open the borders and legalize everyone living in America illegally to cement a permanent majority. 3. Increase the size of the Supreme Court to gain an immediate majority. This would result in America becoming a permanent one-party state and the end of democracy in any meaningful sense of the word. All that is needed to ensure this doesnât happen is 51 Republican senators in 2029. That is why you should vote for Republican senators this election. title: Trump seeks prosecution of Democrat Mary Peltola over alleged scheme to field Dan Sullivan namesake in Alaska
text: US President Donald Trump. US President Donald Trump has called for the removal and prosecution of Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola after a report alleged that people linked to her campaign discussed recruiting a candidate with the same name as Republican Senator Dan Sullivan to potentially confuse voters in Alaska. Alaska Governor Mike Dunleavy has also announced plans to launch a criminal investigation into whether the alleged scheme violated state election laws. The controversy follows a New York Times report published on Wednesday that cited interviews, text messages and documents indicating that Peltola's campaign aides and officials linked to the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC) discussed recruiting candidates named Dan Sullivan to run against the Republican incumbent. Trump called for Peltola and Daniel J Sullivan Jr, a retired schoolteacher who is challenging Senator Sullivan, to be removed from the ballot and prosecuted. In a social media post, he accused Democrats of election fraud and described the alleged operation as voter fraud. Dunleavy said he was directing Alaska's Department of Public Safety to investigate whether the alleged plan warranted criminal charges or civil action. âDeliberately tricking voters into casting their ballots for someone else strikes at the integrity of our elections,â the governor said, adding that anyone found to have broken the law must be held accountable. The allegations have surfaced days before the November 3 midterm elections, with the Alaska Senate race among the contests that could determine control of the US Senate. What the report alleged According to the New York Times, the effort began in 2025, when a Peltola aide was asked to identify Alaskans named Dan Sullivan. The newspaper reported that campaign aides and senior Democratic operatives discussed recruiting candidates who could potentially split support for the Republican senator. The effort eventually focused on Daniel J Sullivan Jr, a retired schoolteacher from Petersburg, Alaska, who has no previous political experience. He qualified for the November general election after the Alaska Supreme Court overturned a state elections official's decision to disqualify him from the primary ballot. The official had concluded that his candidacy had been filed with the purpose of confusing or misleading voters. However, the state Supreme Court ruled that he was qualified to run. The Times report cited interviews with Peltola's former campaign manager, Elisa Rios, and other people familiar with the alleged plan. Rios told the newspaper that Peltola knew about the operation but did not participate directly. The newspaper also reported that Rios later sought to retract her statements. Peltola's campaign has denied involvement in recruiting either Sullivan candidate. The DSCC has also denied recruiting Daniel J Sullivan Jr, despite the report's account of discussions between committee staff and Peltola's campaign. Daniel J Sullivan Jr has maintained that he entered the race independently and had no contact with Peltola's campaign. Political and legal fallout Republican Senator Dan Sullivan's campaign accused Peltola, her advisers and Democratic operatives of colluding to mislead voters. Alaska Senator Lisa Murkowski, who has endorsed Sullivan and is a longtime friend of Peltola, also called for an explanation from the Democratic candidate. The controversy comes as the Trump administration pursues a separate legal challenge seeking to block certification of a possible Peltola victory, citing the presence of the second Dan Sullivan on the ballot. However, legal experts said the allegations reported by the Times would not necessarily affect the outcome of that lawsuit. They noted that while recruiting candidates to split an opponent's vote can be viewed as a dirty political tactic, it is generally legal. The two Sullivans are among four candidates contesting the Alaska Senate seat under the state's ranked-choice voting system, in which voters rank candidates by preference and votes can be transferred when a candidate is eliminated. Peltola, a former Alaska congresswoman, is challenging Sullivan as Democrats seek to win control of the Senate in the November midterm elections. You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. title: US midterms 2026: Trump admin files lawsuit over Alaska Senate race, seeks to block results if GOP loses
text: US President Donald Trump The Trump administration has filed a federal lawsuit seeking to prevent Alaska from certifying its US Senate election results if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan loses, arguing that a candidate with the same name could confuse voters. The lawsuit, filed on Thursday in federal court in Anchorage, claims Alaska would fail to protect election integrity if it certified results affected by the presence of Daniel J. Sullivan on the ballot. He is challenging Dan S. Sullivan, the Republican senator seeking re-election. Daniel J. Sullivan, who previously worked for the US Forest Service and as an elementary school teacher, filed his candidacy on May 29. His campaign website says he is running to unseat the incumbent and âput Alaska firstâ, using the slogan âDan Sullivan Challenges Dan Sullivan for US Senate Seatâ, as cited by Reuters. In interviews with US news outlets, he has denied that his candidacy is intended to mislead voters or draw support away from the incumbent. The lawsuit argues that the similarity between the candidatesâ names could affect the election outcome. The administration is seeking to stop certification if the state determines that the results have been influenced by the presence of the second Sullivan on the ballot. The legal challenge comes as the Senate race draws attention in Alaska, a state that President Donald Trump won by about 14 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election. Recent polling has shown Democratic candidate Mary Peltola level with or slightly ahead of incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan. The race is unfolding amid voter concerns over rising diesel and petrol prices and an unpopular conflict in the Middle East, factors that have contributed to a decline in Trumpâs approval ratings. The lawsuit puts the question of candidate name confusion at the centre of a closely watched Senate contest, with the outcome potentially affecting the balance of power in Congress. text: Hyderabad: Chief minister A Revanth Reddy on Sunday said just as the 'Vanara Sena' assisted Lord Ram in defeating Ravana, Congressâ own Vanara Sena is now fighting to defeat Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his govt, and they will not rest until victory is achieved. title: US judge Alvin Hellerstein, who handled Maduro trial and Trump's hush money case, dies at 92
text: Alvin Hellerstein presides over Maduro's trial proceedings US federal judge Alvin K Hellerstein, who presided over cases involving Venezuelan leader NicolÃ¡s Maduro, President Donald Trump's hush money case and the September 11 terror attacks. Hellerstein died on Wednesday morning surrounded by his family, Chief Judge Laura Taylor Swain said in a statement. He had served on the US District Court for the Southern District of New York since 1998 and continued hearing cases until his death. Swain described him as a âdistinguished juristâ, praising his âenergetic and dedicated serviceâ to the court. âHe is greatly appreciated and will be sorely missed,â she said, as quoted by AP. Hellerstein had continued to preside over Maduro's case despite questions about his age and health. Just two weeks before his death, he oversaw the arraignment of Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, on additional torture charges linked to their ongoing narco-terrorism conspiracy case. Maduro and Flores were captured during a US military raid in Caracas in January. When Maduro twice declined to enter a plea, Hellerstein directed that one be recorded on his behalf. âA plea of not guilty will be entered on behalf of Mr. Maduro,â he said. The judge had scheduled the trial for next June. Analisa Torres, a federal judge who previously served on the Manhattan state bench, will take over the case. She was also part of an international monitoring delegation for Venezuela's 2006 presidential election, won by Maduro's predecessor and mentor, Hugo ChÃ¡vez. Maduro's lawyer, Barry Pollack, said, âWe were saddened to learn of Judge Hellersteinâs passing and offer our condolences to his family.â Key cases handled by Hellerstein Hellerstein's nearly three decades on the federal bench brought him into contact with some of the most consequential legal disputes in the United States, from the aftermath of the 9/11 attacks to presidential immunity and international human rights cases. Trump's hush money conviction: In one of his final significant rulings, Hellerstein rejected Trump's attempt to move his New York hush money case to federal court and have the conviction dismissed on presidential immunity grounds. The case concerned a $130,000 payment to adult film actor Stormy Daniels before the 2016 election. âPaying hush money to an adult film star or engaging in a cover-up of an embarrassment are not subsumed in presidential immunity,â Hellerstein wrote in August. It was the third time he had rejected Trump's efforts to move the case to federal court. The ruling left Trump's conviction in place. September 11 lawsuits : Hellerstein oversaw civil litigation brought by victims and survivors of the September 11, 2001, attacks, including claims involving deaths, injuries and property damage. The cases continued for decades and became a defining part of his judicial career. In 2010, he had rejected a proposed settlement worth at least $575 million for thousands of people who had fallen ill after working amid toxic dust from the World Trade Center site. âThis is different,â he said while explaining why he was intervening in the settlement process. âThis is 9/11.â Lawyers said he spent hours meeting victims and their families and pushed back against settlement offers he considered inadequate. Trump and Michael Cohen: In 2020, Hellerstein ordered the release of Michael Cohen, Trump's former lawyer and fixer, from prison after the Justice Department revoked his home confinement. Cohen had argued that the move was intended to prevent him from publishing a book or speaking to the media. Hellerstein ruled that the government's action was retaliatory and violated Cohen's First Amendment rights. Sudan and BNP Paribas: In a 2025 civil case, Hellerstein presided over a trial in which a jury ordered French bank BNP Paribas to pay nearly $21 million to three Sudanese plaintiffs. The lawsuit alleged that the bank helped sustain the government of former Sudanese ruler Omar al-Bashir by providing access to the US financial system while atrocities were being committed. Abuse of detainees: In 2015, Hellerstein ordered the US government to release photographs documenting the abuse of detainees in Iraq and Afghanistan, another ruling that placed government accountability under scrutiny. His docket also included the criminal trials of Charlie Javice, convicted of defrauding JPMorgan Chase, and hedge fund founder Bill Hwang, convicted in 2024 of securities and market manipulation fraud. From military lawyer to federal judge A New York native and Columbia Law School graduate, Hellerstein served in the US Army's Judge Advocate General's Corps from 1957 to 1960 before entering private legal practice in Manhattan. Then-president Bill Clinton nominated him to the federal bench in 1998. He assumed senior status in 2011 but continued to handle a substantial caseload. His rulings sometimes challenged the government and powerful institutions, including the Trump administration. Hellerstein also blocked the administration in 2025 from deporting alleged Venezuelan gang members without court hearings. You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

title: 82% disapprove of Trump. So why are fewer Indian-Americans identifying as Democrats?
text: US midterms are set to be held on November 3 At an Indian restaurant in Irving, near Dallas, Democratic US Senate candidate James Talarico tried his hand at making a masala dosa , spreading batter on a hot pan and filling it with spiced potatoes. In Connecticut, Governor Ned Lamont joined Diwali celebrations, while Republican Congressman John James visited a Swaminarayan temple in Michigan. From dosas to Diwali and temple visits, politicians from both parties are making symbolic overtures to Indian-American voters ahead of the November 3 midterms. But the communityâs political allegiances are not as straightforward as those campaign gestures might suggest. At the national level, Republicans are fighting hard to retain control of both chambers of Congress. And the odds, at least in prediction markets, are not in their favour. As of October 30, betting website Kalshi gave Democrats a 92% chance of taking control of the House of Representatives and a 69% chance of winning the Senate. Polymarket's corresponding figures were 94% and 72%. A Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on October 26 also found Democrats leading Republicans 47% to 36% among registered voters. Losing control of either chamber, or in the worst case both, could severely hamper US President Donald Trump 's legislative agenda in the final two years of his presidency. So the stakes couldn't be higher . With the Trump administration pursuing what many see as anti-immigration policies, the stakes are also fairly high for the 5.2 million people of Indian origin living in the US. However, there is an interesting paradox between their voting patterns and declared political affiliations. While most are strongly anti-Trump, many don't identify as Democrats. The party's perceived leftward tilt appears to be one source of discomfort among some Indian-Americans. An AP-NORC and AAPI Data survey released on October 19 found that 82% of Indian-American respondents disapprove of Trump's job performance. Yet four in ten held an unfavourable opinion of the Democrats. A separate series of surveys by the Carnegie Endowment earlier in the year suggests that fewer Indian-Americans identify as Democrats than they did six years ago, while more describe themselves as independents. Trump gets thumbs down Together, the surveys challenge the idea of Indian-Americans as a politically uniform community. They reveal differences across age, education, income and other factors that shape political affiliation. A clear Democratic lead The AP-NORC/AAPI Data survey, conducted from September 8 to 15, found Trump's handling of the economy similarly unpopular: 81% disapproved and 18% approved. On immigration, 70% disapproved of his performance. Almost in lockstep, the Republican Party was viewed favourably by only 19%, while 70% held an unfavourable opinion of it. Democrats were in a substantially stronger position, with 51% viewing the party favourably. That advantage also appears in surveys measuring voting intentions. The 2026 AAPI Voter Survey, conducted by AAPI Data and APIAVote between June and July, found that 66% of Indian-American registered voters preferred Democratic candidates for the House of Representatives, against 18% favouring Republicans. Democratic Senate candidates also attracted 66%, compared with 22% for Republicans. Fewer are calling themselves Democrats According to the Carnegie Endowment's 2026 Indian-American Attitudes Survey, conducted between November 2025 and January 2026, the share of Indian-American adults identifying as Democrats declined from 52% in 2020 to 48% in 2024 and 46% in 2026. Over the same period, Republican identification rose from 15% to 19%, while independent identification increased from 23% to 29%. Republicans' gains came between 2020 and 2024; between 2024 and 2026, their share of party identifiers remained unchanged at 19%. The independent share, meanwhile, rose four percentage points. The two-point dip in Democratic identification during this period is small relative to the survey's margin of error. Being independent, however, does not mean being undecided, particularly given the two-party nature of US politics. Carnegie found that the independent share dropped from 29% to 17% when respondents were offered the option of leaning towards one of the two parties. The ideological picture offers another clue. Carnegie found that 32% of Indian-Americans identified as moderates in 2026, up from 28% in 2024. The share selecting the specific label 'liberal' declined from 25% to 21%. But when those identifying as slightly liberal and extremely liberal are included, the broader liberal segment has changed little over the past six years. Rather than indicating a conservative shift, Carnegie describes the community as broadly centrist, with a left-of-centre tilt. Fewer Indian Americans identify as Dems On a scale of zero to 100, the Democratic Party's average rating in Carnegie's survey fell from 60 in 2024 to 53 in 2026. The Republican Party's rating also dropped, from 41 to 34. The decline extended to leading political figures. Kamala Harris's average rating fell from 62 to 52, while Trump's dropped from 40 to 32. Exhausted, but engaged There is another striking finding from the AAPI Voter Survey. Although 92% of Indian-American registered voters said they planned to vote in November, 66% said they always (29%) or often (37%) felt exhausted when thinking about politics. At the same time, 43% described themselves as more enthusiastic than usual about voting in the midterms, compared with 22% who were less enthusiastic, perhaps because a lot more is at stake now. Three-quarters of respondents said they had discussed politics with family or friends in the previous year. Another 25% had discussed politics or community issues through group messaging platforms such as WhatsApp, while 24% had posted about politics on social media. But direct party outreach tells a different story. Forty percent of Indian-American registered voters reported receiving no contact from the Democratic Party over the preceding year, while 56% said the same of Republicans. The Democratic drift is not uniform Carnegie's findings also challenge the idea that younger Indian-Americans are necessarily moving away from Democrats. Among respondents aged 18 to 29, Democratic identification increased from 51% in 2024 to 56% in 2026. Among those aged 50 and above, however, it declined from 47% to 39%. Education produced another divide. Democratic identification among respondents without a college degree fell from 48% to 35%, while remaining broadly unchanged among college graduates, at 49%. Income revealed a similar split. Among Indian-Americans in households earning between $50,000 and $99,999 annually, Democratic identification declined from 54% to 44%. Among those in households earning at least $100,000, it increased from 46% to 51%. Gender differences were also visible. Democratic identification among men fell from 46% to 40%, while among women it rose slightly, from 50% to 52%. So older Indian-Americans appear to be moving away from identifying as card-carrying Democrats, although the trend among the well-off is different. Economy remains the big issue In the September AP-NORC/AAPI Data poll, 87% of Indian-American respondents identified the economy as one of the most important election issues. Cost of living followed at 84%, while 76% said the same of healthcare. Despite weaker party identification, Democrats enjoyed sizeable advantages on these issues. Fifty-three percent trusted Democrats more to handle the economy, compared with 12% who trusted Republicans. On the cost of living, the corresponding figures were 52% and 8%. On healthcare, Democrats held an even larger advantage, with 60% trusting them more, against just 6% for Republicans. But these preferences did not amount to universal confidence in the party. On the economy, 20% trusted neither party. On the cost of living, the proportion was 25%. Economy to healthcare: Democrats enjoy a clear lead Democrats also had an advantage on immigration in the September survey, with 50% trusting them more, against 18% who preferred Republicans. On crime, however, the numerical gap was narrower: 29% trusted Democrats more and 19% Republicans, while 28% trusted neither. India ties not a major concern Inflation and prices were the single most important policy issue for 21% of respondents in Carnegie's survey, followed by jobs and the economy at 17%. Healthcare ranked next at 13%, followed by immigration at 11%. Only 2% named USâIndia relations as their top concern. That is perhaps along expected lines, though many in India probably view Indian-Americans' political behaviour through the prism of the IndiaâUS bilateral relationship. For most desis living in the US, it is not the top concern. The finding does not mean that Indian-Americans are indifferent to relations between Washington and New Delhi. It means that domestic issues, particularly economic concerns, matter more when respondents are asked to identify their single most important policy priority. Is the Democratic Party's leftward tilt a problem? Carnegie asked respondents who did not identify as Democrats to rank their top two objections to the party. The most frequently cited reason, at 19%, was the perception that Democrats were too influenced by their left wing. Concerns about the party's approach to illegal immigration and disagreements with its economic policies followed at 17% each. Another 16% cited perceptions that Democrats were too soft on crime, while an equal share objected to what they considered excessive emphasis on identity politics. These issues overlap with broader conservative criticism of what is often called liberal or 'woke' politics. The findings suggest that the Democratic Party's perceived leftward tilt makes it harder for some Indian-Americans to identify with the party. But there is another side to this argument. The same Carnegie survey found that 68% of Indian-Americans who were familiar with Zohran Mamdani were enthusiastic about his election as New York City mayor, while 22% were unenthusiastic. Among those enthusiastic about his victory, 44% cited the expectation that he would govern as a liberal or progressive. Among those unenthusiastic, 36% said he was too liberal or progressive. Even among Indian-Americans identifying as Republicans, enthusiasm and opposition to Mamdani's victory were almost evenly divided, at 44% and 45%, respectively. That makes the political picture more complicated. Some Indian-Americans regard the Democratic Party as too influenced by its left wing, while others welcome the rise of progressive politicians such as Mamdani. The question beyond November 3 There are important limitations to these findings. The relatively small ethnic subgroups surveyed carry greater statistical uncertainty than the surveys' overall samples. Carnegie's historical survey waves also involved different respondents and changes in sampling methods, so the reported shifts do not establish that individual voters have switched party allegiance. What the surveys do show is a distinction between candidate preference and party identity. Democratic candidates continue to enjoy a large advantage. Trump's job performance is viewed negatively by a substantial majority. Beyond the midterms, the challenge for Democrats will be to sustain their electoral support among Indian-Americans while addressing the concerns of those who no longer identify strongly with the party. Attention will eventually turn to the nomination contests ahead of the 2028 presidential election. The continuing influence of the MAGA movement within the Republican Party, and the ideological direction of the Democrats, will be among the factors shaping the political choices facing Indian-Americans. For now, though, the polling suggests that many desis would like to give Trump the electoral blues. You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

title: Omar Abdullah faces internal storm: Many NC MLAs upset over J&K cabinet rejig; Srinagar MP announces resignation
text: Omar Abdullah and Farukh Abdullah (File photo) SRINAGAR: The government of chief minister Omar Abdullah is facing signs of discontent within the ruling National Conference (NC), with a number of legislators reportedly unhappy over the recent cabinet expansion and seeking greater democracy within the party and resignation of the whole cabinet. The discontent within the party has taken place at a time when the party MP from Srinagar Aga Ruhullah Mehdi is resigning from the party on November 3 leaving Srinagar parliamentary seat open. âI will resign from the National Conference and my Lok Sabha seat on November 3, 2026. The crown prince and his cabal treat J&K as an estate passed down through the family. They expect the people to vote, then know their place. They take us for fools who cannot tell a broken promise from a political necessity. Ask them to honour their own manifesto, and they lecture us on how little we understand realpolitik,â Mehdi wrote on X. Watch Omar Abdullah Moves Full Statehood Resolution In J&K Assembly, BJP Protest Sparks House Uproar âWe demanded the restoration of Article 370, the release of prisoners and the protection of our rights. They sought power on those promises, then treated us as fools for expecting them to deliver. We refuse to lend our name to this humiliation. There is no fixing this rot from within. The seat was won on a promise to the people,â Mehdi added. Mehdi said he would surrender the seat rather than become an accomplice to the betrayal of that promise. Mehdi would address the people on November 3, the death anniversary of his father, Aga Syed Mehdi, at Behisht-e-Zehra Park in Budgam. His father was a Congress leader and prominent Shiite cleric who was assassinated in a terrorist attack on November 3, 2000. Ruhullah Mehdi is an alumnus of Tyndale Biscoe School and holds a bachelor's degree in arts from the University of Kashmir. His political career began in 2002, when he contested and won his first Assembly election from Budgam. He retained the seat in 2008 and 2014. In 2009, he was inducted into the state Cabinet, becoming the youngest Cabinet minister. In 2015, Mehdi was nominated as the chief Spokesperson of the National Conference, the position he held for several years. However, after abrogation of Article 370 on August 5, 2019, he distanced himself from the partyâs stand of maintaining silence over the situation in Jammu and Kashmir after August 5. He would urge the party to take a stand on Article 370 rather than urging the centre to restore statehood which he describes as a scaled down position. In August this year the NC president Dr Abdullah said Mehdi would not have won the parliamentary elections without the NC support. He said that if Mehdi believed Article 370 could be restored, he should fight for it, as no one had stopped him from pursuing the cause. Dr Abdullah had said the NC had not prevented Mehdi from pushing for the restoration of Article 370. Dr Abdullah had said Mehdi should resign and contest elections on his own. In response Mehdi had said that Dr Abdullah has for the first time asked anything from him and he will not disappoint him. MLAs meeting Meanwhile, according to the sources, over a dozen party legislators met Friday evening at the residence of Qaiser Jamshaid Lone, who represents the Lolab constituency, with several others joining the meeting online. They decided to seek resignation of the entire council of ministers and demand that a new cabinet be formed through consensus, based on merit and in keeping with democratic principles, sources said. They also decided to seek the resignation of the chief ministerâs advisor Nasir Ahmad Wani. In a related development, NC president Dr Farooq Abdullah removed Mubarak Gul as the partyâs general secretary. Gul was among the MLAs who attended the meeting at Loneâs residence. After the cabinet expansion on Tuesday, Dr Abdullah had elevated Gul, who wanted cabinet induction for himself, to the post of general secretary. Omar Abdullah and Dr. Farooq Abdullah are in New Delhi. Dismissing reports of widespread discontent within the party and rebellion, NC spokesperson Ifra Jan questioned the claim that 20 MLAs attended the meeting at Loneâs residence. âThey are saying 20 MLAs held this particular meeting. Where is this figure of 20 coming from? Is there a photograph or a list of names? Somebody anonymously claims 20 and everyone else repeats it without any investigative corroboration,â she said. âAfter the cabinet expansion, I think one or two MLAs openly expressed their displeasure and that was there for everyone to see. Isnât that normal? Doesnât this happen in all political parties? Some MLAs are happy while others are unhappy. This is common practice across the country,â she said. âEver since Omar Sahib (Omar Abdullah) took oath, the leader of the opposition BJP's Sunil Sharma, has been claiming that the government will fall next week. Unfortunately, nobody is asking why. Every disagreement is being viewed through the prism of âgovernment will fall rumoursâ without any evidence. We consider any claim of large-scale discontent within the party as a rumour,â she added. Sunil Sharma said it seems Omar Abdullah government has only eight MLAs with it and those eight are cabinet Ministers. Nazir Gurezi, who was part of the meeting, told the TOI that Lone had invited all MLAs and âlarge number of MLAs were at his residence. We just had food thereâ. On Tuesday morning Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha administered the oath of office and secrecy to the newly inducted ministers, Ali Mohammad Sagar, Shamima Firdous, Mir Saifullah and Altaf Ahmad Kaloo at Lok Bhawan in Srinagar taking the number to eight with Omar including nine. Omar dropped Satish Sharma, who was Minister for food, consumer affairs, transport science, IT, youth affairs, sports, and training. Omar was sworn in as chief minister on October 16, 2024, along with five ministers. Under the prescribed norms, the council of Ministers cannot exceed 10% of the total strength of the legislative assembly. With 90 members, the Jammu and Kashmir Assembly can have a maximum of nine ministers, including the chief minister. Three cabinet berths had remained vacant for nearly two years as the party struggled to decide whom to induct. Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines Soon after the expansion on Tuesday, NC MLA Abdul Majeed Larmi broke down. âI deserved a place in the cabinet. I felt very sad not to be part of the cabinet. I was deserving of it (cabinet seat). Till the last moment, I was expecting to be part of the cabinet,â Larmi said. âI am a law graduate, while the MLA chosen has not even passed matriculation,â he had said. Mubarak Gulâs supporters lodged a protest at the party headquarters. In the 90-member Assembly, the NC has 41 MLAs and is backed by six independent legislators, while the Congress, with six MLAs, extends support to the government from outside. title: ECI takes stock of UP poll preparations ahead of 2027
text: The Election Commission of India (ECI) reviews preparations for 2027 UP assembly polls at a meeting in Meerut, attended by bureaucrats of 18 districts of Western UP Meerut: The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Monday reviewed preparations for the 2027 UP assembly elections at a meeting in Meerut, assessing poll preparedness in 18 districts across four divisions -- Meerut, Saharanpur, Moradabad and Aligarh. The meeting, chaired by senior deputy election commissioner Manish Garg, was attended by UP chief electoral officer Navdeep Rinwa and other senior officials from the CEOâs office. Divisional commissioners, police commissioners, inspectors general and deputy inspectors general of police, district election officers, and senior superintendents of police and superintendents of police from the districts concerned also participated. Officials from the 18 districts made presentations on election preparedness, management and administrative arrangements, outlining the progress of measures undertaken so far. âThe Election Commission has taken steps to ensure transparency across all processes, including the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), SSR and continuous updation of electoral rolls,â Garg said. He said the rationalisation of polling stations in UP had been completed as part of the SSR exercise. District magistrates had shared the details with representatives of all political parties, and the proposals had subsequently been forwarded to the CEOâs office and then to the Election Commission. âThe draft electoral roll will be published on Nov 12. Copies will be provided to political parties, while the draft rolls will also be uploaded on the website for public access. Anyone can examine the lists and file objections,â Garg said. He added that the claims and objections process would continue for a month, after which Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) would take final decisions in accordance with the law. The final electoral rolls would also be shared with all political parties and displayed on the official website and at polling stations, he said. The 18 districts covered in the review were Meerut, Baghpat, Bulandshahr, Gautam Budh Nagar, Ghaziabad, Hapur, Saharanpur, Muzaffarnagar, Shamli, Amroha, Bijnor, Moradabad, Rampur, Sambhal, Aligarh, Etah, Hathras and Kasganj. title: US midterms 2026: Polling guru Allan Lichtman, who accurately predicted 9 of last 11 presidential races, sees headwinds for Democrats
text: Historian Allan Lichtman/Image: Getty Images Historian Allan Lichtman, who predicted nine of the last 11 US presidential elections correctly, expects Democrats to take control of both chambers of Congress in next week's midterm elections, forecasting a setback for President Donald Trump's Republican Party. Lichtman, a professor at American University in Washington, DC, said national polling, Trump's approval ratings, voter enthusiasm and early voting trends indicate that Democrats are gaining ground ahead of the November 3 elections. In an interview with The Times (UK), Lichtman said the political environment was particularly unfavourable for Republicans, pointing to the president's low approval ratings and the historical losses suffered by the party controlling the White House during midterm elections. "When the approval rating for a president is as low as Trump's, on average the White House party loses 40 House and six Senate seats," Lichtman said. He clarified that the figures were not his prediction but an indication of the political conditions facing Republicans. Lichtman said Democrats currently hold an advantage of seven to 11% points over Republicans in the generic congressional ballot, which measures voter preferences for which party should control Congress. He considers this measure a more reliable indicator than polls focused on individual races. He also pointed to a shift in voter enthusiasm. While Republicans typically record higher turnout, Lichtman said Democrats appeared more motivated this time. He added that early voting figures were also favourable to the party. The historian puts Democrats' chances of winning control of the Senate at 67%, with a 51-49 majority his most likely outcome. Republicans currently hold a 53-47 advantage in the Senate, meaning Democrats need a net gain of four seats to take control. Lichtman expects the party to make gains in Maine, North Carolina, Ohio and Texas while retaining its seat in Michigan. He also identified Alaska as a potential Democratic pickup, with former Representative Mary Peltola among the candidates he expects to benefit. He pointed to the competitiveness of races in traditionally Republican states as another indication of the changing political landscape. "It's amazing that Democrats are competitive in South Carolina, which Trump won by 18 points," he said. "Kansas has not sent a Democrat to the Senate since the Great Depression in 1932 and yet that's a neck-and-neck race, as is Iowa." Lichtman also expects Democrats to take control of the House, where Republicans currently hold a narrow 218-214 majority. He puts the party's chances of winning the chamber at more than 90%. He attributed some of the Republican Party's difficulties to what he described as weak candidates, naming Ken Paxton in Texas, Roger Marshall in Kansas and Darline Graham in South Carolina. The historian also criticised the influence of wealthy donours and outside spending in the election campaigns. He argued that large financial contributions were affecting the political contest and pointed to billionaire Elon Musk's support for Republican candidates. Lichtman compared the current political climate to the 1966 midterm elections, when Democrats suffered major losses under then-President Lyndon B Johnson amid growing opposition to the Vietnam War and domestic unrest. His latest assessment comes after he incorrectly predicted that Democratic candidate Kamala Harris would defeat Trump in the 2024 presidential election. He also missed the outcome of the 2000 race between Al Gore and George W Bush. You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

title: Karnataka MLC polls: Big setback for DK Shivakumar as BJP-led NDA wins all 4 seats
text: BENGALURU: In a major setback to the ruling Congress and chief minister D K Shivakumar, the BJP-led NDA won all four Karnataka Legislative Council seats that went to polls on October 23, sweeping both teachersâ and graduatesâ constituencies. The NDA fielded three BJP candidates and one JD(S) candidate. JD(S) candidate A P Ranganath defeated Congress veteran and five-time MLC Puttanna in the Bengaluru Teachersâ constituency, while BJP candidate Shashil G Namoshi registered his fifth victory in the North-East Teachersâ constituency, defeating Congress nominee Sharanappa Mattur by 3,297 votes. Namoshi secured 15,596 first-preference votes against Matturâs 12,299. Counting concluded at Kalaburagi, where around 30,253 voters had exercised their franchise. Of the votes counted, 28,380 were valid, while 1,873 were rejected. In the graduatesâ constituencies, BJP candidates SV Sankanur and KM Suresh also emerged victorious, completing the NDAâs clean sweep of all four seats. In the West Graduatesâ constituency, Sankanur secured his third consecutive victory, defeating Congress rival Mohan Limbikai. In the other graduatesâ constituency, BJP candidate KM Suresh won the seat, ensuring that the NDA did not concede any ground to the ruling party in the elections. This is the second biennial legislative council election since Shivakumar became chief minister on June 3. In the June 18 elections to seven council seats from the MLAsâ quota, Congress won five seats and the BJP secured two. However, the ruling party failed to replicate that performance in the teachersâ and graduatesâ constituencies. Ranganath won the Bengaluru Teachersâ constituency on his third attempt, defeating Puttanna by 908 votes. He secured 10,810 first-preference votes against Puttannaâs 9,902. Ranganath had lost to Puttanna in the 2022 and 2024 elections. This time, he capitalised on a sympathy wave to secure victory. Puttanna had contested as a BJP candidate in 2022 before switching to Congress for the 2024 by-election. title: Civic polls to test NDAâs popularity, YSRCPâs revival bid in Visakhapatnam
text: The election is being closely watched as results in a politically neutral city such as Vizag are often seen as an indication of public mood. Pic: SS Vijay Babu Visakhapatnam : The Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) election on Su nda y, Nov 1, is set to witness a keen contest between the NDA and YSRCP. The mayor seat has been allocated to the TDP as part of the seat-sharing arrangement among the TDP, BJP and Jana Sena . The election is being closely watched as results in a politically neutral city such as Vizag are often seen as an indication of public mood. The verdict is expected to offer insights into perceptions of the TDP-led govtâs performance, which will complete two and a half years in Dec, and oppositionâs role. With a sizeable, educated and politically aware electorate, the city is also expected to send a message on governance and civic issues. While the outcome in individual wards has attracted limited attention, the main focus is on the two mayoral candidates and the message voters may deliver through their mandate. The TDP is looking to continue its winning streak from the 2024 elections, when it secured a nearly five lakh majority in the Vizag MP constituency. The YSRCP, meanwhile, is equally determined to win the mayorâs post. The TDP has fielded first-time corporator Mukka Sravani, while the YSRCP has nominated senior politician and MLC Varudu Kalyani. The election has also become a prestige battle for the MLAs, as most corporator candidates are their loyalists. The MLAs played a key role in securing tickets for their supporters, making the civic polls a test of their political influence. The ticket distribution has also led to rebel candidates entering the fray, including those who have worked in their respective wards for years or had high hopes of securing party nominations. The seat-sharing arrangement among NDA partners has not gone down well with a section of their cadre. With the TDP winning all assembly seats and the two Lok Sabha constituencies partly falling under GVMC limits in 2024, local MLAs and MPs have campaigned aggressively in their respective areas. The YSRCP, which faced relatively fewer internal disputes over seat allocation, focused on reaching out to voters. Its mayoral candidate, Varudu Kalyani, a seasoned politician, actively campaigned across the city. Though 15 candidates are in the race for the mayorâs post, the main contest is between the TDP and YSRCP. The two parties have also adopted contrasting approaches in their manifestos. The NDA has focused on infrastructure development and improved civic services, while the YSRCP has centred its campaign on the âSave Vizagâ theme and pollution- and environment-related concerns. The NDA has listed nine commitments, including better drinking water supply, underground drainage, roads and street lighting. The YSRCP pledged to address drinking water shortages by improving reservoirs and ensuring a regular supply. It also promised to revive 12 proposed flyover projects, improve roads and drainage, upgrade 42 urban health centres and introduce a grievance redressal app. YSRCP mayoral candidate Varudu Kalyani said the party would protect the cityâs natural resources, environment, public assets and heritage, while ensuring that residents are not burdened with additional taxes. âWe will develop Vizag to place it among the top cities in the country. The TDP has failed to fulfil its promises even after 30 months in power,â she said. TDP mayoral candidate Mukka Sravani said a mandate for the alliance would accelerate development and improve civic services in Vizag. âIf elected, I will consider the position an opportunity to serve the people and take the city forward on all fronts,â said the former corporator. GFX Polling will be held from 7 am to 5 pm on Sunday, Nov 1 A total of 18,37,901 voters will exercise their franchise. 1,990 polling stations established across GVMC limits. 14,334 polling personnel deployed for election duties. 15 candidates in the fray for the mayorâs post. Main contest between the NDA and YSRCP. 573 candidates contesting for 120 corporator positions. Election material distribution centres established in all 10 zones. Gajuwaka has the highest number of polling stations at 329. 82 returning officers and assistant returning officers appointed for election duties. title: US midterms 2026: Judge blocks Trump admin from threatening election workers over voter data demands
text: US President Donald Trump A US federal judge has barred the Justice Department from threatening state and local election officials with prosecution for refusing to follow the Trump administration's demands over voters suspected of being non-citizens. US District Judge Trina Thompson issued the temporary restraining order on Friday, ruling that the administration could not use its list of alleged non-citizen voters to direct local officials to change how they administer elections. The order prevents the federal government from demanding that election officials remove voters from state registration lists, reject ballots from specific voters or separate ballots cast in the midterm elections on the basis of the administration's list. Thompson said the Justice Department had overstepped by threatening prosecution against officials who did not cooperate with its election-related initiatives. The ruling followed a lawsuit filed by election workers' unions and other groups. "The balance of the equities and public interest weigh in Plaintiffs' favor," Thompson wrote, citing the need for election officials and workers to perform their duties under federal law and established election procedures. The decision comes days before the November 3 midterm elections. Republicans currently hold narrow majorities in both chambers, while Democrats are seeking to gain control of the House and potentially the Senate. The Trump administration has sought voter-registration data from states, arguing that stricter oversight is necessary to protect election security and public confidence in the voting process. However, its efforts have drawn criticism from election officials and political experts, who have raised concerns about federal interference in state and local election administration. Some election officials told Reuters they were preparing for possible federal intervention during the midterms. Trump has repeatedly questioned the integrity of US elections and continued to make false claims about the 2020 presidential election, which he lost to former President Joe Biden. title: 5th term for Harjinder Singh Dhami or Bibi Jagir Kaurâs return? SGPC to elect president on Nov 20
text: In the 2025 SGPC presidential election, Dhami (L) secured 107 of the 142 votes polled during the general house meeting. Jagir Kaur (R), who also contested for the post, received 33 votes. AMRITSAR: Will Harjinder Singh Dhami secure a fifth consecutive term as Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) president, or will the November 20 election bring a change of guard? Amid growing discontent over the SGPCâs management, insiders said an impression was being created that Dhami was no longer keen to continue as president. Meanwhile, speculation that former SGPC president Bibi Jagir Kaur could return to the Badal-led Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and reclaim the top post has added another dimension to the electoral contest. Jagir Kaur had parted ways with the Sukhbir Singh Badal-led SAD and joined the Shiromani Akali Dal (Punar Surjit). The SGPC executive committee met on Friday and convened a general house session at 12 noon on November 20 at Teja Singh Samundri Hall, the committeeâs headquarters, to elect its president and other office-bearers for the coming year. A senior Akali source said the election could prove a significant political test for the Sukhbir-led SAD, which holds a majority in the SGPC general house, particularly as the party seeks to consolidate its position ahead of the 2027 assembly elections. âThe central question is whether Dhami will secure a fifth consecutive term as SGPC president or whether the SAD leadership will spring a surprise by bringing another face,â sources said, adding that Jagir Kaur could also return to the top post despite having left the Badal-led SAD for SAD (Punar Surjit). In the 2025 SGPC presidential election, Dhami secured 107 of the 142 votes polled during the general house meeting. Jagir Kaur, who also contested for the post, received 33 votes. Panthic affairs expert Jagdeep Singh said Dhami had remained relatively less controversial than his predecessor, Jagir Kaur. âDhamiâs decisions have generally received wide appreciation, whereas Jagir Kaurâs tenure was marked by several controversies,â he said. Jagdeep added that Dhamiâs relatively low-profile functioning and ability to maintain working relations within Panthic circles could work in his favour. However, he said the outcome would also depend on political equations within the SAD and the choices made by its leadership. Another source did not rule out a possible rapprochement between the two Akali factions, which could open up fresh possibilities for the SGPC leadership. Recent reports of discussions involving SAD (Punar Surjit) leaders over a possible broader Akali-BJP political arrangement for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections have added another dimension to the developments. However, there is no confirmed agreement on the return of any particular leader to the Badal-led SAD or on a possible SGPC candidature. title: US judge dismisses charges against 2 ex-FBI officials over Hunter Biden laptop probe, calls prosecution 'weaponisation'
text: Hunter Biden, the son of former US President Joe Biden/Image: AP A US federal judge has dismissed criminal charges against two former FBI officials accused of making false statements to Congress about the investigation into a laptop belonging to Hunter Biden, citing serious flaws in the Justice Department's handling of the case and concerns over its political timing. US Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui dismissed the complaint against Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides on Monday, saying the investigation was rushed and marked by procedural errors. He described the prosecution as an instance of âweaponizationâ and questioned the circumstances under which the case was opened. âWhat has transpired here cannot be described as anything other than weaponization,â Faruqui said during the hearing as cited by AP. The judge noted that the investigation began a day after President Donald Trump delivered a televised speech revisiting his grievances over the 2020 election. He also pointed to FBI Director Kash Patel's involvement, saying the investigation had been mandated by Patel and closely monitored by him. Faruqui questioned why prosecutors had waited until two weeks before the midterm elections to bring charges over statements made by the former officials in 2023, despite having had the opportunity to pursue the case earlier. âI will not bury my head in the sand and pretend that I cannot read a calendar,â the judge said. The ruling followed a hearing in which Faruqui criticised prosecutors over their handling of the proceedings. An FBI agent involved in the investigation also testified that he had worried the case could be viewed as politically motivated. The complaint accused Floris and Benavides of misleading lawmakers in 2023 about their involvement in, and knowledge of, efforts to investigate a laptop that Hunter Biden reportedly left at a computer repair shop in Delaware in 2019. The case also revisited Republican allegations that the FBI had attempted to suppress information about the laptop during the 2020 presidential campaign because it could damage the Biden family's political standing. Joe Biden, the Democratic candidate, defeated Trump in that election. The Justice Department's filing referred to a 2020 briefing given by Floris and Benavides to lawmakers. Republican Senators Chuck Grassley of Iowa and Ron Johnson of Wisconsin have alleged that the briefing was intended to undermine their investigation into the Biden administration and associate it with Russian disinformation. Faruqui had questioned the legal approach taken by prosecutors from the outset. He raised concerns about the decision to proceed through a criminal complaint rather than seek a grand jury indictment, a route generally used when authorities need to take a defendant into custody quickly. At a preliminary hearing last week, the judge also criticised prosecutors for submitting an amended complaint overnight that added another criminal charge without first obtaining the court's approval. He said he had not encountered such a procedure before. The judge's dismissal does not necessarily end the case. According to the report, the Justice Department could still seek a grand jury indictment against the two former officials. However, the ruling marks a setback for prosecutors, particularly as the department has faced difficulties securing indictments in politically sensitive cases in Washington. During the hearing, an FBI agent who worked on the investigation testified that it had been opened after Trump delivered a speech on election security last July. The agent said FBI Director Kash Patel had ordered the inquiry and closely monitored its progress. Faruqui's decision came two weeks before Tuesday's midterm elections, a timing that featured prominently in his criticism of the prosecution. The judge questioned why the department had chosen to bring the case at that point rather than when the alleged statements were made in 2023. You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. title: Imran Khan tenders unconditional apology in HC over anti-SIR protest participation
text: NEW DELHI: Actor Imran Khan on Monday tendered an unconditional apology after the Bombay high court reprimanded him for participating in a protest against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls despite being a US citizen. A bench led by Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra questioned how the United States would have reacted if an Indian national had protested there. "What for were you there? There's a complete difference between the rights of citizens and OCI card holders... You need to clarify whether you were there for protests or for some other work. You will have to categorically make a statement that you had no association with the protests, etc. Because the agitation was with regard to SIR, with which you have no concern at all," the court said. Watch Actor Imran Khan Asked To Leave India By Oct 28: Can An OCI Cardholder Be Deported For Protesting? "Obviously, because you aren't an Indian citizen... Imagine if an Indian citizen does such protests in any other country, take, for example, your country - the US. That Indian citizen would have been sent back to the country on the next immediate flight," the court added. Following Khan's apology, the Bombay high court scheduled the next hearing for December 7 and kept the "Leave India" notice against him in abeyance until then. The Bombay high court was hearing Khan's plea challenging a Leave India Notice (LIN) issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO), directing him to leave India by October 28. The court had earlier kept the notice in abeyance until November 2 and has now extended the relief until December 7. title: 25 in fray for 7 PUTA posts, final list of candidates out
text: Representational image Patna : The battle lines have been drawn for the Patna University Teachersâ Association (PUTA) elections, with 25 teachers in the fray for seven key posts after the final list of valid candidates was published on Wednesday following scrutiny and withdrawal of nominations. Polling is scheduled for Nov 4. The contest is particularly crowded for the posts of general secretary and joint secretary. While five candidates are vying for the lone post of general secretary, 10 teachers are contesting the two joint secretary posts. The presidential race features four candidates: Shankar Kumar (Physics), Kumar Satyendra Yadav (PG Department of Statistics), Sheo Sagar Prasad (IPRS) and Supriya Krishnan (PMIR). For the two vice-president posts, Archana Jaiswal, Salim Jawed and Suppan Prasad Singh are in the fray. The five candidates contesting for general secretary are Ashutosh Kumar, Ashutosh Pandey, Birendra Kumar, Deep Narayan Kumar and Shekhar. The treasurerâs post will witness a three-cornered contest among Naqui Ahmad John, Jyoti Chandra and Md Ziaul Hassan. The election will also decide the composition of PUTAâs executive committee. The final list includes 23 candidates for 19 executive committee positions. While several constituencies have uncontested candidates, elections will be held in others. In an attempt to make the campaign issue-based, the central election committee has organised separate debates for presidential and general secretary candidates on Oct 31 at Jay Prakash Narayan Anushad Bhawan. Candidates will be given equal opportunities to present their vision, priorities and programmes before the teaching community. Polling will be held from 10am to 3pm on Nov 4 at the Patna College gymnasium, with nearly 400 teachers expected to cast their votes. The election assumes significance as PUTA is going to the polls after a gap of more than three years. The last election was held in July 2023. title: Is Jagan Reddy's 'regret' message a calculated alliance pitch for Congress?
text: A successful alliance with the INDIA bloc hinges on the YSRCP and Congress aligning, which could be Jagan Mohan Reddyâs biggest challenge NEW DELHI: Is YSRCP supremo YS Jagan Mohan Reddy signalling a drift towards the Congress-led INDIA bloc? Or is he trying to break free from the image of being soft on the BJP ? The former Andhra Pradesh chief minister has provided issue-based support to the BJP-led NDA government on several key legislations in Parliament while he was in power in the state. However, he has stayed away from joining any alliance till now. So, when Jagan Reddy recently regretted his âmistakeâ of supporting the 2023 NDA legislation for selecting the Chief Election Commissioner, it fuelled speculation about his future political moves. "We regret supporting the process under which the ruling party nominates the Chief Election Commissioner at the Centre. Neither the CEC nor the SEC should be appointed by the ruling party. The selection committee should comprise the Prime Minister, the leader of the opposition and the Chief Justice of India (CJI), with all three exercising their voting rights," the YSRCP chief said recently, calling the current selection system "flawed. " The timing and context of Jaganâs remarks are significant. So, is he rethinking his âsoloâ politics? And if yes, will the Congress be ready to tango with him in Andhra Pradesh? After all, alliances with regional parties have been the Congressâs biggest Achilles heel across states. Jaganâs support for NDAâs key Bills Jagan Mohan Reddyâs MPs backed the Modi government several times between 2019 and 2024, both in Lok Sabha and in Rajya Sabha, on many important legislations. However, when it came to stitching an alliance for the 2024 elections, the BJP ignored Jaganâs help and joined hands with his arch-rival Chandrababu Naidu. Together, TDP and BJP swept the polls in Andhra Pradesh, winning 164 out of 175 seats in the assembly and 21 out of 25 seats in Lok Sabha. The YSRCP was reduced to 11 seats in the assembly and 4 in Lok Sabha. Despite being spurned by the BJP and his partyâs shock defeat, Jagan Mohan Reddy remained confident about his BJP ties. After all, he still had 15 MPs (4 in Lok Sabha and 11 in Rajya Sabha) to provide the much-needed support to the BJPâs minority government at the Centre. Jagan even announced that his MPs would extend issue-based support to the NDA government in matters concerning national and state interest. But with the BJP heavily dependent on Chandrababu Naiduâs support for survival of its government at the Centre, there was little room for the saffron party to accommodate Jagan Reddy. Nearly two and a half years down the line, Reddy seems to have accepted this harsh reality and is perhaps gearing up to chart a new path for the next political challenge in 2029. Jagan vs Congress However, for any successful alliance with the INDIA bloc - the YSRCP and the Congress will have to be on the same page. And that perhaps would be the biggest challenge for Jagan Mohan Reddy. Jagan Mohan Reddy had a bitter parting from the Congress in 2010, a year after the death of his father YS Rajasekhara Reddy. YSR Reddy was in his second term as the chief minister of Andhra Pradesh when he died in a helicopter crash on September 2, 2009. Jaganâs supporters, who were many in number, lobbied hard with the Congress high command for the top post, but Sonia Gandhi did not budge and made K Rosaiah the chief minister. The Congress leadership did not approve of Jaganâs Odarpu Yatra, which was part of his announced plan to meet the families of many people who had sacrificed their lives after his fatherâs death. That set the stage for his eventual exit from the Congress, which he announced on November 29, 2010 in an open letter to Sonia Gandhi carefully written to ensure there was enough public sympathy for his second phase of political career. In the 2014 assembly elections, the YSRCP made an impressive debut and won 67 out of the 175 seats with a vote share of 44.46%, while the Congress could manage only a vote share of 2.8%. The Congress decision to bifurcate the state and create Telangana played a huge role in the partyâs declining political fortunes in the state. On November 6, 2017, Jagan embarked on the Praja Sankalpa Yatra and covered 3,648 km in 341 days, crossing 134 assembly constituencies. The Yatra, from YSR Ghat at Idupulapaya to the northeastern tip of Ichchapuram, powered Jagan Mohan Reddy to a historic mandate of 151 seats in the 175-member assembly in the 2019 elections. The Congressâs vote share was reduced to less than 1%. The Congress, since then, has been making efforts to reclaim its lost political space in the state. It roped in Jagan Reddyâs sister Y S Sharmila as part of the partyâs revival plan. Sharmila, who started her political career with her brother Jagan Mohan Reddy eventually drifted towards the Congress and was appointed president of Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee in January 2024. However, both Jagan Mohan Reddy and his sister Y S Sharmila failed to make an impact in the 2024 elections. The 2024 elections saw a dramatic collapse of Jaganâs electoral fortunes, and his party was reduced to only 11 seats. The Congress once again failed to make its presence felt. The 2029 challenge And that brings us to the 2029 elections - a do-or-die challenge for both Jagan Mohan Reddy and the Congress. Jaganâs remark on backing the CEC appointment Bill is his first open âregretâ for backing the BJP. But does this âopen regretâ mean an olive branch for the Congress? Former Congress leader and senior political commentator Sanjay Jha strongly feels that Jagan and Congress should come together, though he admits that this may not be easy. âPolitics is the art of the possible and I'm sure Jaganmohan Reddy is aware that Chandrababu Naidu has been an extremely close alliance partner of the Modi government. While the Congress doesn't have a base in Andhra like it used to have once upon a time. The support base of Jaganmohan Reddy is basically the Congress vote which moved away from the traditional Congress to the Congress that Jaganmohan Reddy, branded as the Congress of his father. So, if the merger were to happen, it would, frankly speaking, give them a huge advantage because then both the Central Congress and the Jaganmohan Congress could be on the same page,â Sanjay Jha says. However, he accepts that merger of the two parties could be a difficult process while stitching an alliance may be easier. âOnce a political party becomes independent and has power, they don't like to give it up in a hurry. The TMC or the NCP are good examples. In which case it could be an alliance,â Sanjay Jha adds. The third option, according to Sanjay Jha, is for the Congress to resurrect itself on its own strongly in Andhra by capturing both the anti-incumbent votes against Chandrababu Naidu and winning back the loyalist voters of the Congress who had moved over to Jaganmohan Reddy. Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines This is easier said than done. The Congress has a poor track record when it comes to winning back states it has lost. We have seen several states across the country where the Congress has lost its government and eventually its support base but does little to reclaim it. In Andhra Pradesh, Chandrababu Naidu and the BJP are going all out to consolidate their position. Naiduâs call for greater cooperation and coordination among southern states at a recent conference is perhaps an effort to keep his importance and relevance intact. We saw DMKâs MK Stalin make similar moves before he lost power to Vijayâs TVK in the last assembly elections. Jagan Mohan Reddy and the Congress face an uphill electoral battle in 2029. It will be interesting to see if they can agree to an alliance to take on Chandrababu Naidu and the BJP. title: Three days to deadline, guidelines issued for IOA's SOM nominations
text: New Delhi, Oct 10 (IANS) The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) has begun its 2026 electoral process under the National Sports Governance Act, 2025, with the Athletesâ Commission election scheduled for November 3 and the Executive Council polls set for December 5. NEW DELHI: The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) Electoral Officer (returning officer), Sanjay K. Srivastava, has issued guidelines for the Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOM) elections, warning that nominations that fail to comply with the prescribed conditions will not be considered valid. In the document dated October 26, retired IAS officer Srivastava clarified the nomination procedure and issued a modified Form 2 for candidates seeking election as SOMs to the IOA General Assembly. The deadline remains October 30. Watch Bombay Sport Exchange: Mustafa Ghouse on ISL, India's sporting ecosystem and grassroots problem The revised instructions place particular emphasis on the role of proposers and seconders, who must be members of the male or female SOM roster published by the Electoral Officer on October 23. An individual can propose or second one candidate in the male category and one in the female category. However, if the same person endorses more than one candidate in either category, the later nomination will be rejected. The instructions also state that a proposer or seconder cannot withdraw their name once the nomination has been delivered. The rules permit cross-gender endorsements: a male SOM can propose or second a female candidate, and a female SOM can do the same for a male candidate. The restriction is on endorsing multiple candidates within the same category, not on the gender of the candidate being nominated. Eight representatives to enter the IOA General Assembly PT Usha The SOM election will determine eight representatives to the IOA General Assembly, comprising four men and four women. Under the IOAâs Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit Rules, 2026, one male and one female representative will subsequently be elected from among the eight to the IOA Executive Council. The SOM framework is designed to incorporate the experience of former elite athletes, including the current president PT Usha , into the governance of Indian sport. Candidates must satisfy the prescribed eligibility conditions, including Indian citizenship, being of sound mind, being between 25 and 70 years of age on the date of application, and having retired from active sport for at least one year before applying. They must also have represented India in an Olympic sport for which the concerned national sports federation or sports body is an IOA member. title: âWhy did Congress lose three elections in a row?â Kiren Rijiju poses five questions ahead of INDIA bloc's 'Delhi Chalo' rally

Meanwhile, Rijiju further asked whether all sitting Congress chief ministers would resign and whether the party would apologise for forming governments between 2014 and 2026, if it had won elections despite alleged manipulation in the BJP's favour. title: Imran Khan apologises, Bombay high court extends relief on Leave India notice
text: Actor says he will not take part in any future stir MUMBAI: Bombay High Court on Monday continued its interim relief against Centreâs Leave India Notice to actor Imran Khan Pal (44), a US citizen and an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI), after he furnished a prepared undertaking and added an unconditional apology which the court sought. The central govtâs Foreigner Regional Registration Office (FRRO) had given him two weeks to leave India, four days after registering an FIR against Khan for unlawful assembly in Mumbai during an Oct 10 protest against the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls and the CEC. Additional Solicitor General Anil Singh said the âCentre through the FRRO has unfettered rights to deport such person,â a foreigner (Khan) from India, âwithout the need to establish any jurisdictional fact. â The HC order said: âThe state, in exercise of its sovereign functions, would have the right to deport a person out of India in a given case. To further clarify this aspect and clarify its stand, Centre agreed to file an affidavit.â Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna said, âOCI card holders are not Indian citizens.ââ They were hearing a petition Khan filed to challenge the Leave India notice as arbitrary and in violation of his right to life. âYou cannot behave like an Indian citizen. You are not even remotely associated with the SIR process,ââ said the CJ orally to Khan, via his senior counsel VR Dhond, who said he was ready with the undertaking. âThe right to protest is not even available to you as an OCIâ¦,â added Justice Sethna. Dhond said they are not getting into the legality of the Constitutional rights but under Article 21âright to life and liberty which is available to non-citizens, principles of natural justice do accrue. The CJ asked what was Khan doing at the protest site and how was he connected? âWhat were you there for? There is a complete difference between rights of an OCI card holder and a citizen of India. You will have to categorically make a statement that you have no association with the protestâ¦ you had no remote cause for being thereâ¦ If an Indian was doing this in another country would it have been permissible or tolerated?.â Dhond referring to pleadings in the petition said, âGlad you asked. He (Khan) has no association or affiliation with those who organised the protest against the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC).ââ The ASG for the FRRO tendered a compilation to the bench and argued that it was not an isolated instance and that Khan âinstigatedââ people on social media. Khan has been in India since he was two years old, for the past 42 years, said Dhond having studied here, worked here, married and having a child in India. He should be heard, Dhond argued. The state said an FIR is registered against Khan. Dhond said but neither has the actor been summoned nor called for any probe and all offences, including disobedience of orders and unlawful assembly are bailable. The actor was passing by and was curious to see the protesters as mentioned in the petition, Dhond submitted. âI (Khan) have at the moment no film in hand. Have nothing to do with those who organised the protest. The HC can take an undertaking that I (Khan) have no part in the protest. Before I (Khan) could even reach the site there was a police bandobastâ¦,â Dhond submitted. The ASG questioned the veracity of Khanâs claim over how he landed at the protest spot, saying, âIt is a misleading statement. That out of curiosity he went there to checkâ¦ He is part of the protest.ââ Singh said the actor is a US citizen and the Centre is within its power to expel him. The Centre ârequires no foundational basis to expel a foreigner from the India,ââ said Singh. âHence, there is no question of granting any protection. He takes all the benefit as a citizen of the US and as your lordship just said, Article 19 doesnât apply to OCI. The (FRRO) has taken a decision to remove a foreigner. It is the Centreâs discretion. A visa too doesnât mean a foreigner has all the rights to enter India.â âIf you read the petition the impression given is thatâ¦ he was curiousâ¦ but see he has given an interviewâ¦,â Singh submitted. The HC sought a reply from the Centre. âIt is better that you (Centre) respond. Khan will have a chance to file a rejoinder. We can then decide the matter,ââ said the bench. The bench remarked, âThis case is purely distinguishableâ¦ He has on his OCI registration said he is unemployed.ââ The judges said to Khan, âWhy donât you accept India citizenship? You work and live here. You make films here. You are a celebrity. Why donât you apply for Indian citizenshipâ¦ You have to give a categorical undertaking that you will not participate in any such protest as you are an OCI and these are not available to OCI card holders. ââ Dhond tendered the undertaking and the Chief Justice said, âIf this kind of undertaking comes, you have to tender one with an unconditional apologyâ¦You (Khan) have everything and recognition pan India. Your (Khanâs) one statement would have decisive impact (on fans).ââ The CJ Tripathi and Justice Sethna orally said, âIt is least expected. You (Khan) are a responsible person. Literate and highly educated. you come from a responsible family. You have a great following. Since childhood you are in India. And the country has never raised such an issue against you in the pastâ¦you cannot behave or be placed on a par with Indian citizensâ¦ââ The bench on seeing the Centreâs compilation said, âYou cannot say, â I was a novice and had no idea. ââ Dhond sought a copy of the compilation, saying they cannot tender fresh material across the bar. The CJ said, âInadvertently if you had participated then there should be regret on oath. You (Khan) had no role at all in the SIR. Whatever statement you have made. You should make an unconditional apology. We will record in the order.ââ The ASG said, âThis undertaking and apology is by a foreigner as an OCI holder falls within definition of a foreigner. This is not merely a question of participation in a protest The CJ at one point said smilingly, Khan has lived here for so long that he â forgot that perhaps you are an OCIââ. The CJ recorded that Khan has tendered an unconditional apology and posting the matter to Dec 7 at 3 pm said in the end to Khanâs counsel, âyou must tell your client that filing an apology doesnât mean it is a green signal to say or do anything...You can go to the USA and cast your vote and participate in protests there...â You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in Mumbai Stay updated with the latest Mumbai news.
