title: âI am here. With youâ: Nobel laureate, Venezuela opposition leader Machado returns after nearly a year in exile
text: File photo: In this photo released by Vente Venezuela Press Office, Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado greets supporters at a church in Barquisimeto, Venezuela Venezuelan opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize laureate MarÃ­a Corina Machado returned to Venezuela on Sunday after nearly a year in exile. Her team confirmed her return, in a move likely to increase pressure on interim president Delcy RodrÃ­guez as the countryâs political future remains uncertain. âI am here. With you,â Machado wrote in Spanish on X, without disclosing how she had re-entered the country or providing details of her whereabouts. Her close ally, exiled opposition leader Edmundo GonzÃ¡lez Urrutia, also confirmed her return in a social media post. âVenezuela! I am thrilled to announce to you that our leader, my dear MarÃ­a Corina, is on Venezuelan soil,â he wrote, adding that he would return soon. Machado was later seen at a church in Barquisimeto, the capital of Lara state, about 220 miles west of Caracas. Footage and photographs published by news organisations showed supporters greeting and embracing her during a religious ceremony at the Sanctuary of the Divine Shepherdess. Machadoâs exile Machado left Venezuela covertly in December 2025 to receive the Nobel Peace Prize in Norway. Since then, she has made several attempts to return, but Venezuelan authorities blocked her entry, according to her party and her advisers. Her return comes amid continuing uncertainty over the countryâs political transition following the removal of former president NicolÃ¡s Maduro by US forces in January. Machadoâs opposition movement is widely believed to have won the 2024 presidential election, although Maduro was declared the winner and refused to hand over power. GonzÃ¡lez, who stood in the election after Machado was barred from running, has been living in exile. Following Maduroâs ouster, RodrÃ­guez, his former vice-president, assumed the role of interim president with the backing of US president Donald Trumpâs administration. Washington has prioritised economic stabilisation and access to Venezuelaâs oil, while Machado and her allies have pressed for a date for fresh presidential elections. The Guardian reported that the Trump administration had opposed Machadoâs return, fearing it could complicate its relationship with RodrÃ­guez. However, Trump told reporters on Sunday that he did not know about Machadoâs return, adding that he hoped she was safe. âSheâs a very nice woman,â he said, referring to the Nobel Peace Prize medal Machado had given him. US secretary of state Marco Rubio said the circumstances that enabled Machadoâs return were the result of US support for reconciliation talks. In a post on X, Rubio said Washington expected the freedoms of all sectors of Venezuelan politics to be respected and urged political actors to support negotiations aimed at achieving free and fair elections. Machadoâs homecoming comes as her party continues to demand an electoral timetable. RodrÃ­guezâs interim administration has held rounds of negotiations with a section of the opposition and agreed to judicial reforms, but no date for a presidential election has been announced. Machado has repeatedly praised Trump for the operation that removed Maduro and presented him with her Nobel medal during a meeting in January. Her return now puts renewed focus on whether Venezuelaâs political transition will lead to competitive elections and what role the opposition will play in shaping the countryâs future. title: US intelligence confirms image shows China's secret spaceplane in orbit; design resembles X-37B
text: The US Defense Intelligence Agency has unveiled a detailed satellite image showcasing China's experimental reusable spaceplane currently in orbit The US Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) has confirmed that a satellite image released in a newly declassified report shows China's experimental reusable spaceplane in orbit, offering a clearer view of a spacecraft whose design closely resembles the US Space Force's X-37B. The higher-resolution image, captured by a satellite operated by Maxar Technologies, now known as Vantor, was included in the DIA's latest unclassified assessment of security challenges in space, released on October 26. Although a lower-resolution version had circulated publicly since 2024, the spacecraft's identity had not been confirmed at the time. Watch Project 18A: Indiaâs â¹75,000 Crore Plan for Bigger, Deadlier Next-Gen Navy Destroyers The image shows a compact, shuttle-like vehicle with wings, twin vertical tails, an open payload bay and a rear-mounted module with solar panels deployed on either side. Its overall configuration resembles the X-37B, an uncrewed reusable spaceplane operated by the US Space Force, although the Chinese vehicle appears to have longer wings. âA key capability for reusable space activities are spaceplanes like this PRC [Peopleâs Republic of China] Spaceplane captured by Maxar. Spaceplanes can launch into orbit to place objects in space or even test them and return to earth [sic],â reads the caption to the picture in DIAâs report. The exact date and circumstances of the satellite's observation have not been publicly disclosed in the DIA report. However, the image carries a 2024 copyright date, placing it within the period when China's spacecraft was conducting its third orbital mission. China has conducted four spaceplane missions since 2020 China is understood to have conducted four orbital missions using its experimental reusable spaceplane since 2020. The latest mission began on February 7, 2026, and the spacecraft remained in orbit as of the latest available reports. The vehicle's activities have attracted attention because it has reportedly released smaller objects into orbit and carried out operations involving other spacecraft. During its third mission, which lasted from December 14, 2023, to September 6, 2024, the spaceplane was observed releasing multiple smaller objects. Their identities and purposes remain unknown. Analysis of open-source orbital tracking data by astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell also indicated that the spacecraft involved in the latest mission released and subsequently recaptured a smaller object during a series of orbital operations. These activities point to its ability to interact with objects in space, although its precise mission objectives remain undisclosed. The spacecraft is commonly referred to as Shenlong in Western reports, but its official designation and the model shown in the image have not been definitively established. The DIA report states that âChina has two primary spaceplane models: the Shenlong and Tengyun,â without specifying which one appears in the photograph. China's Shenlong programme has been discussed publicly since at least 2007, when images emerged of what was believed to be a prototype or test vehicle mounted beneath an H-6 bomber. Separately, the state-run China Aerospace Science and Industry Corporation unveiled its Tengyun reusable spaceplane concept in 2016. The proposed system was designed around a two-stage-to-orbit approach involving a carrier aircraft, rather than relying entirely on a conventional rocket launch. It remains unclear whether the planned Tengyun test targeted for 2025 took place. How China's spaceplane compares with the US X-37B The Chinese vehicle shares several visible design features with the US Space Force's X-37B, including a winged body, payload bay and a configuration intended to support a return to Earth. Both spacecraft are uncrewed and designed for reusable orbital operations. The US has built two X-37B vehicles, which have flown a total of eight orbital missions since 2010. The spacecraft can carry experiments and payloads into orbit before returning to Earth for recovery and refurbishment. Much of its operational activity remains classified. China's spaceplane is also understood to launch aboard a conventional rocket before operating in orbit and returning to Earth for a runway landing. A secretive Chinese airbase in the country's northwest, featuring an exceptionally long runway, has been identified in reporting as a possible landing site for the vehicle, although the full details of its recovery operations remain unclear. The image does not establish whether the Chinese spacecraft carries weapons or is being used for offensive missions. However, its ability to manoeuvre, deploy objects and potentially interact with other spacecraft has raised questions about the military applications of reusable spaceplanes. DIA warns of growing competition in space The DIA's report places reusable spaceplanes within a wider assessment of expanding space capabilities and the potential risks they pose to US and allied assets. In general, âspaceplanes are â¦ reusable and feature enhanced maneuverability, making them more suitable for certain missions than traditional satellites,â DIAâs report notes. Such vehicles can potentially deploy small satellites, conduct experiments, inspect other spacecraft and return payloads to Earth. Their ability to alter trajectories and approach other objects also makes them useful for missions that conventional satellites may find more difficult to perform. The report also discusses China's development of counterspace capabilities, including ground-based laser weapons that could disrupt, degrade or damage satellites in low Earth orbit. âChina has multiple ground-based laser weapons with varying power levels to disrupt, degrade, or damage satellites in LEO,â the DIA said. âBy the late 2020s, China may field space-based directed energy systems and higher-powered ground-based directed energy systems capable of threatening satellites in higher orbits.â The assessment also points to China's testing of ground-based anti-satellite missiles, satellite servicing and refuelling technologies, and robotic systems that could potentially interact with spacecraft in orbit. China has expanded its space-based intelligence and surveillance capabilities in recent years, while the United States and Russia are also developing systems that can manoeuvre close to other satellites. Such activities have raised concerns about the potential for interference with, or attacks on, space assets. The DIA report also explains the economic rationale behind reusable technology, noting that conventional space access has relied heavily on expendable launch vehicles and spacecraft. âIn general, access to space traditionally requires expendable spacecraft: single-use launch vehicles, satellites, and one-time use capsules designed to maximize performance. Reliance on expendable vehicles has made access to space expensive and exclusive,â DIAâs report explains. âReusable technologies, while even more difficult and expensive to develop and build, stand to greatly reduce the cost of spaceflight by recovering, refurbishing, and reusing rocket stages, fairings, and capsules. â The newly released image provides a clearer look at China's experimental spaceplane, but its full capabilities, payloads and intended military role remain unknown. Its resemblance to the X-37B, combined with reported orbital manoeuvres and object deployments, underscores the growing role of reusable spacecraft in the increasingly competitive space domain.

title: US midterms 2026: Trump to campaign for Mike Rogers in Michigan after Obama rally for Abdul El-Sayed
text: US President Donald Trump US President Donald Trump is set to campaign for Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers in Michigan on Sunday, a day after former President Barack Obama urged voters to support Democrats in the state ahead of next week's midterm elections. The visit to Port Huron marks Trump's first campaign appearance in Michigan this year, despite his repeated attacks on Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed. The state's open Senate race is among the most competitive contests and could help determine which party controls the chamber. El-Sayed, who would become the first Muslim elected to the US Senate if he wins, has faced attacks from Trump and Rogers over his religion and alleged links to the Muslim Brotherhood. El-Sayed has denied any affiliation with the group and rejected questions about his loyalty to the United States. Watch Iran Threatens âUnimaginableâ Response; Trump Throws Weight Behind Netanyahu In Israel Poll Battle At a debate last week, Rogers questioned El-Sayed's allegiance, asking whether he supported the United States or what Rogers described as terrorist groups overseas. He has alleged that El-Sayed has ties to the Muslim Brotherhood but has provided no evidence for the claim. El-Sayed has described the accusations as shameful. In a recent campaign advertisement, he defended his faith, saying, "faith is a thing thereâs just too little of in Washington". Obama addressed the controversy during a rally in Detroit on Saturday, arguing that the attacks were intended to portray El-Sayed as less patriotic and less American than his opponents. The former president compared the claims to false allegations about his own birthplace, which had circulated during his political career. "We have seen this movie before," Obama said. "I starred in it ... This stuff didn't work on me. Not in Michigan. It's not going to work on Abdul." Trump responded on Truth Social early Sunday, criticising Obama's support for El-Sayed and describing the Democratic candidate as a "Muslim Brotherhood Jihadist". He also accused El-Sayed of hating Jews, Black people, Americans and Trump, and predicted that he would lose the election. The Michigan contest has also become a point of tension over Trump's trade policies. Port Huron is in an area that Trump won with more than 66% of the vote in the 2024 presidential election. title: California Governor Gavin Newsom warns federal judges of possible ballot seizures ahead of US midterm elections
text: California Governor Gavin Newsom California Governor Gavin Newsom has asked federal judges to remain alert to possible attempts by the Trump administration to seize election ballots and related materials ahead of the 2026 US midterm elections, amid an ongoing legal dispute over federal demands for voter records. In a letter to federal judges on Saturday, Newsom said he was concerned that federal agents could seek search warrants to take possession of ballots before election results are officially certified. âGiven the United States Department of Justiceâs persistence in advancing this baseless theory of criminal liability, I have grave concerns federal agents will seek search warrants to seize ballots and ballot materials before the election results are certified,â Newsom wrote. He argued that such warrants could interfere with California's election process, including the counting of votes and certification of results. The warning follows a series of legal setbacks for the Trump administration in its efforts to obtain California's election records as part of an investigation into alleged noncitizen voter registration. On Friday, a US appeals court rejected the administration's latest attempt to block the state from counting votes allegedly cast by noncitizens. The dispute centres on the Justice Department's claim that more than 20,000 noncitizens are registered to vote in California. However, state officials and election experts have questioned the accuracy of the federal government's list. The Justice Department has not disclosed how many people identified in its records have actually cast ballots. California officials have described the information as unreliable, arguing that complying with federal demands could result in eligible voters being wrongly removed from the electoral process. A separate federal court ruling has also restricted the administration's approach. A judge ordered the Justice Department to stop threatening criminal prosecution against state and local election officials who refuse to comply with its election-related demands. The dispute has raised questions over the federal government's authority in administering elections. The US Constitution gives states responsibility for conducting elections, while the Trump administration has pursued access to voter records through its investigation into alleged noncitizen registration. title: Amitabh Bachchan pays emotional tribute to Sanjay Gupta: âCompanions from the world of art are being snatched awayâ
text: Sanjay Gupta , the filmmaker who gave audiences 'Kaante', 'Kaabil' and 'Shootout at Wadala', passed away on October 30 at the age of 59, reportedly after a fall in the bathroom of his Mumbai home. Amitabh Bachchanâs blog post on Sanjay Guptaâs demise Reacting to the filmmakerâs death, Amitabh shared a heartfelt post on his blog on Sunday. title: 'Will be game over for America': Elon Musk raises three 'concerns' against Democrats ahead of midterms
text: Musk urged people to vote for Republicans Billionaire entrepreneur Elon Musk backed Republicans on Friday and warned that a Democratic sweep of the US House of Representatives, Senate and presidency in 2028 could lead to what he described as the âend of democracy in any meaningful sense of the wordâ, ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. In a series of posts on X on Thursday, Musk outlined three changes he fears Democrats could pursue if they gain control of the White House and both chambers of Congress: granting statehood to Washington DC and Puerto Rico, legalising people living in the US illegally, and expanding the Supreme Court. âMy biggest concern is that if there is a clean sweep by Democrats of the House, Senate and Presidency in 2028, they will,â Musk wrote, before listing the three possibilities as: 1. Make DC and Puerto Rico states to gain a strong majority in the Senate. 2. Open the borders and legalize everyone living in America illegally to cement a permanent majority. 3. Increase the size of the Supreme Court to gain an immediate majority. He then added: âIt would be game over for America.â Musk argued that the changes would allow Democrats to consolidate their political power and turn the US into a âpermanent one-party stateâ. He called on voters to ensure Republicans retain at least 51 Senate seats in 2029, saying: âThat is why you should vote for Republican senators this election. Other reasons are irrelevant compared to this one.â His remarks come just days before the US midterm elections, which will determine control of Congress for the final two years of President Donald Trump's term. Republicans currently hold narrow majorities in both chambers, but Democrats are seeking to regain control amid voter concerns over inflation, the economy and the administration's policies The billionaire's warning comes amid a broader political battle over the balance of power in Washington. Statehood proposals for Washington DC and Puerto Rico, immigration policy and the possibility of expanding the Supreme Court have been subjects of political debate, with significant disagreement between the two parties. Musk's millions for Republicans Musk has emerged as one of the biggest financial backers of Republicans in the 2026 midterm elections. The Washington Post reported on October 23 that he had contributed about $446 million to influence the election cycle, largely through Republican-aligned political action committees. His contributions include substantial funding for the Senate Leadership Fund, which supports Republican Senate candidates, and America PAC, his own political action committee. He has also backed efforts to help Republicans retain control of the House. The spending marks a renewed push by Musk to influence US politics after his public falling-out with Trump last year. Why are the 2026 midterm elections crucial? The November 3 elections will determine which party controls the House and Senate for the final two years of Trump's presidency. A change in control could significantly affect the administration's legislative agenda, spending negotiations and congressional oversight. Republicans hold a narrow majority in the House and a 53-47 advantage in the Senate. Democrats need net gains in both chambers to take control. Recent polling has favoured Democrats in the race for the House, while the Senate contest remains more uncertain. A Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted through October 26 put Democrats ahead of Republicans by 53% to 44% among likely voters on the generic congressional ballot. A CBS News/YouGov poll also projected Democrats on course for 229 House seats, although Republicans retained a narrow path to holding the chamber. The elections are being fought against a backdrop of concern about the cost of living and Trump's handling of the economy. A recent AP-NORC poll found that about 80% of voters identified the economy or cost of living as a major election issue. Even if Democrats win one or both chambers, their ability to enact major legislation would remain constrained by Trump's veto power and other institutional checks. title: US midterms: FBI, ICE agents will not serve as election monitors, DOJ says
text: FBI agents will not be "monitoring" midterm polling booths The US Department of Justice said FBI and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) personnel will not serve as monitors during the November midterm elections, amid concerns from civil rights groups that the Trump administrationâs plans for federal election oversight could intimidate voters. In a court filing late Wednesday in a lawsuit brought by the NAACP, the Justice Department said federal election monitors would observe polling places, take notes and would not act as law enforcement personnel, reported Reuters. They would also be prohibited from carrying firearms and have been trained not to interfere with voting or violate state and local rules, the filing said. While employees of the Federal Bureau of Prisons, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) and the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) will serve as monitors, the department said neither FBI nor ICE employees would be deployed in that role. Concerns over the possible deployment of federal law enforcement officers at polling sites had grown in the run-up to the midterms. Last month, a coalition of civil rights groups led by the NAACP sued the Trump administration, seeking to prevent ICE agents and other federal law enforcement personnel from being stationed at polling locations. The groups argued that the prospect of such a deployment could intimidate voters, particularly Black, Latino and Asian communities, naturalised citizens and members of mixed-status families. Even President Donald Trump declined to rule out sending ICE officers or National Guard personnel to polling locations. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin had said ICE would not patrol polling sites but could respond if there was a threat at a location or agents needed to serve a warrant. The Trump administration has also stepped up scrutiny of voter registration records, pressing states for voter data and arguing that stricter oversight is necessary to maintain confidence in elections. Some officials told Reuters this month that they were preparing for potential federal interference in the midterms. The Justice Departmentâs filing addresses the role of election monitors, while the broader legal challenges also contest the administrationâs increased scrutiny of voter rolls. The groups argue that the presence, or threat of deployment, of federal officers could amount to voter intimidation and violate protections under federal voting-rights law. You use AI every day. title: Fireworks, flags and celebrations as student-led movement wins in Serbia; can they deliver reforms?
text: In Serbia, can a leaderless student movement, with little experience of governing, turn its electoral victory into lasting political change? Celebrations swept across Serbia after Gen Z-backed candidates defeated president Aleksandar Vucicâs ruling party in a historic election, ending his long grip on power. In Belgrade, crowds filled central squares, cars draped in Serbian flags honked their horns and fireworks lit up the sky as jubilant protesters dismantled barricades around a pro-government encampment near parliament. But beyond the celebrations, a key question remains: Can a leaderless student movement, with little experience of governing, turn its electoral victory into lasting political change? Watch ON CAM: Celebrations & Chaos! Political Earthquake In Serbia As Vucic Loses; Serbia Streets Go Wild The election follows nearly two years of student-led demonstrations sparked by the collapse of a canopy at the Novi Sad railway station in 2024, which killed 16 people. Protesters blamed corruption and cronyism for the disaster, turning the tragedy into a wider campaign for accountability. From street protests to political power Visuals circulating on social media showed crowds taking to the streets of Belgrade and other Serbian cities soon after the election results were announced. The student movement built nationwide support without a single leader and eventually fielded 250 candidates, including academics, lawyers, doctors, farmers, actors and musicians. Its agenda centres on anti-corruption measures, judicial reform and stronger public institutions. The candidates have proposed an independent police unit accountable to prosecutors, transparent appointments to state-owned companies and tighter scrutiny of public infrastructure contracts. However, unity could prove difficult once the movement begins governing. â(The student movement created) such a shift in Serbia's culture; we will just have to see if it lasts,â Katarina Popovic, a professor at the University of Belgrade told news agency Reuters. âWe just hope that there are big goals that can keep them together long enough to deconstruct the system,â she added. Can the new government deliver reforms? Under Serbiaâs constitution, the student-backed candidates have 90 days to form a government after parliament is convened following the announcement of final election results. The immediate challenges include passing a year-end budget, addressing rising public and private debt, reforming the police and intelligence services, and strengthening the judiciary. The students' victory "is likely to trigger broad institutional and policy changes centred on anti-corruption, the rule of law, and better public services. However, bureaucratic resistance to reforms and the movementâs limited governing experience could make the transition challenging," Teneo Global Research said in a report on Monday. The IMF projects Serbiaâs economy to grow 3 per cent in 2026 and 4 per cent in 2027, while inflation rose to 4.1 per cent in September from 2.2 per cent in August. The central bank has held its benchmark interest rate at 5.75 per cent since 2024. âThe new government would have to fight its corner,â warned Bozo Prelevic, a Belgrade-based lawyer and former co-minister of the interior, referring to the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), which is expected to remain a formidable opposition force. The movement has also promised economic changes, including action against retail monopolies to lower food prices, tax relief for lower-income groups, affordable housing initiatives and cheaper medicines. Kosovo, Russia and the European Union Foreign policy could be another test. The student-backed candidates oppose recognising Kosovoâs independence, declared in 2008, while relations with the European Union remain strained over stalled accession talks and the need to normalise ties with Pristina. The movement has also said it does not intend to impose sanctions on Russia, Serbiaâs traditional ally and a major gas supplier. At the same time, the European Commission has offered support for reforms involving the rule of law and media freedom. âI am sure (the Student List) will find a way, just as they have so far, to choose someone capable of governing,â said Savo Manojlovic of the student-friendly Move-Change movement, according to Reuters. title: 4 lakh voters aged above 85 years across Karnataka
text: Belagavi district has the highest number of voters and tops the list in Karnataka Mysuru: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has identified nearly four lakh voters aged above 85 years across Karnataka , with five southern districts accounting for about 17% of the total. Belagavi district, which has 18 assembly constituencies, has the highest number of voters aged 85 years and tops the list in Karnataka. Mysuru is second with 25,165 such voters, followed closely by Tumakuru with 24,665, placing these three districts in the top three in terms of senior citizen voter concentration. Mandya has 16,263 voters in the 85+ category, while Hassan has 15,923 in fourth and fifth places. To ensure greater inclusion, the ECI introduced home voting for the first time in a Lok Sabha election in 2024, extending the facility to voters above 85 years of age and persons with disabilities (PwDs) with 40% benchmark disability. The option is meant for those who face difficulties in visiting a polling station. The eligible voters must inform polling officials in advance to avail themselves of home voting. Karnataka has a substantial number of elderly voters Karnataka, which has 224 assembly constituencies, has 33,92,134 voters as per ECI data. Alongside the large overall electorate, the state has a substantial number of elderly voters, requiring targeted planning at the booth level. ECIâs arrangements for home voting add an additional layer of coordination for election officials, particularly in districts with a higher concentration of 85+ voters. Dakshina Kannada and Kalaburagi have more than 14,000 voters each in this age group. Bengaluru Urban has around 13,007, while Dharwad has 10,117 and Bengaluru South has 10,443. Among the smaller districts in this category, Chamarajanagar has 7,943 elderly voters and Kodagu has 4,044. Mysuru illustrates the operational scale required to implement home voting smoothly. The district accounts for about 6.4% of Karnatakaâs 85+ voter base, and officials have to identify and facilitate eligible voters across nearly 2,900 polling booths in 11 assembly constituencies. This requires advance communication, verification and logistical deployment to ensure that home voting is conducted securely and within election rules, while also enabling elderly voters and PwDs to participate with dignity and minimal physical hardship. title: Trump admin asks Supreme Court to set aside 20,000 California ballots over citizenship row a day before midterms
text: US President Donald Trump The Trump administration has asked the US Supreme Court to intervene in a dispute over approximately 20,000 mail ballots in California, arguing that votes cast by people suspected of not being US citizens should be kept aside until their eligibility can be verified. The emergency appeal was filed on Monday, a day before the midterm elections, AP reported. It followed an appeals court decision rejecting the administration's request to set aside the ballots, which belong to voters whose citizenship status the federal government has questioned. The Justice Department has argued that California should prevent the disputed ballots from being counted until officials establish whether the voters are eligible. State authorities have challenged the reliability of the federal government's list, saying it is likely to include many US citizens. The dispute centres on the administration's efforts to identify suspected noncitizen voters, even though such cases are rare. The Justice Department has asked the Supreme Court for a limited injunction directing California to stop mixing the disputed ballots with those cast by eligible voters while the legal proceedings continue. California has been conducting its elections by mail since early October. The state sends ballots to all its approximately 23 million registered voters, and hundreds of thousands of ballots have already been processed. Lower courts have so far ruled in favour of California. A district court judge rejected the Justice Department's request, warning that separating the ballots could prevent eligible citizens from having their votes counted in the midterm elections. US District Judge David O. Carter said segregating the ballots could âwreak havocâ on the election and undermine public confidence in the democratic process. Carter, who was nominated by former President Bill Clinton, also warned against allowing unproven allegations to affect an ongoing election. âIf the Executive can discount votes and threaten an ongoing election due to unproven allegations, then our democracy is in danger,â Carter wrote. The Justice Department has attempted to accelerate the case, including by asking an appeals court to intervene before it had fully progressed through the lower courts. That request was unsuccessful. The latest appeal puts the dispute before the Supreme Court as voting continues across California. The administration has secured several favourable outcomes through emergency appeals to the justices, although the court previously rejected Trump's attempt to restrict mail ballots ahead of the midterm elections. title: Council poll results raise alarm for GA, open space for JSP
text: Policemen stand guard at a counting centre in Patna on Tuesday Patna : The NDA âs performance in the Oct 23 legislative council elections is certainly a morale booster for CM Samrat Choudhary and JD(U) chief Nitish Kumar âs heir apparent Nishant Kumar, but the results declared on Tuesday may sound an alarm bell to the Grand Alliance (GA) comprising RJD, Congress and Left. The results may also give space to Prashant Kishor âs Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) as people opposed to the BJP look for an alternative, as they did in Bankipur. Prashant, who recently defeated the BJP in its stronghold Bankipur assembly byelection, has been trying to emerge as an alternative to traditional political parties at a time when Gen Z is agitated over the lack of jobs and employment opportunities in the country in general and Bihar in particular. Though graduate and teacher council constituencies are small compared with the electorate in assembly polls, the fact that candidates and voters were either graduates or teachers and considered publicly aware people with discerning judgment made the results significant. While Prashant campaigned for his candidates, RJD national working president and party face Tejashwi Prasad Yadav was conspicuous by his absence during electioneering. The JSP, for the first time since its formation in 2024, contested council polls and fielded candidates on all eight seats at stake. It not only won the Darbhanga Teachersâ seat by defeating sitting Congress MLC Madan Mohan Jha, but also garnered either more or only a few votes fewer than the runners-up in the remaining constituencies. Though RJD had no MLC in any of the eight constituencies in the Oct 23 polls, it was the main opposition party in the last elections. RJD contested seven seats, leaving the Tirhut Teachersâ constituency for ally CPI, which could not retain the seat this time. Congress fielded candidates on five seats, while CPI(M) and CPI(ML) also contested one seat each. Of the eight seats, the NDA held three â Kosi Graduates and Patna Teachers (BJP), and Patna Graduates (JD(U)) â while independent candidates had won three: Tirhut Graduates, Darbhanga Graduates and Saran Teachers. CPI and Congress held Tirhut Teachers and Darbhanga Teachers respectively. A Prashant Kishor-backed candidate, Afaque Ahmad, had won the Saran Teachersâ seat in 2023, giving his campaign its first taste of electoral success. But Afaque lost to independent Rahul Raj, a BJP rebel, this time. title: US midterms 2026: Indian-born Nithya Raman challenges LA mayor Karen Bass
text: Nithya Raman is gearing up to challenge incumbent Mayor Karen Bass in the 2026 mayoral election in Los Angeles. Nithya Raman, an urban planner and Los Angeles City Council member born in India, is challenging incumbent Mayor Karen Bass in the November 3, 2026, election, promising to tackle the city's housing crisis, homelessness and deteriorating public services. Although the contest is taking place alongside the US midterms, it is a municipal election, not a congressional race. Raman moved to the United States with her family at the age of six. She graduated from Harvard University and earned a master's degree in urban planning from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Before entering electoral politics, she worked on homelessness initiatives and co-founded the SELAH Neighborhood Homeless Coalition in Los Angeles. In 2020, Raman defeated incumbent David Ryu to win a seat on the Los Angeles City Council, becoming the first South Asian person elected to the council. She won re-election in 2024 and has focused on housing affordability, tenant protections, homelessness and climate policy. She also served as executive director of Time's Up Entertainment, an organisation addressing sexual harassment in Hollywood. Raman entered the mayoral race in February 2026, despite having previously endorsed Bass. She finished second in the June 2 primary, securing a place in the November runoff against the incumbent. Her campaign proposes increasing housing construction, strengthening renter protections, improving basic city services and expanding unarmed emergency-response services. She has also pledged to protect immigrants and streamline permits to support small businesses. Her campaign faces scrutiny over her changing positions on policing, homelessness programmes and the city's mansion tax. Bass and her supporters have questioned Raman's experience and approach to public safety, while Raman argues that Los Angeles needs a change in leadership and more accountable government. The contest will test whether Raman can turn her progressive support and record on housing into a citywide winning coalition against an incumbent backed by prominent Democrats and much of the City Council. title: US Federal Reserve keeps rates unchanged, leaves door open to further hikes
text: US Fed holds interest rates at 3.75%-4% as inflation persists, signals scope for further hikes The US Federal Reserve held interest rates unchanged at 3.75%-4% in a 10-2 vote, as policymakers weighed persistent inflation against a resilient economy and waited for further data before deciding their next move. The decision came ahead of next weekâs US midterm elections, with the central bank acknowledging that inflation remains elevated despite signs of continued economic strength. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said economic activity was expanding at a âstrongâ pace, upgrading the Fedâs assessment from âsolidâ at its September meeting. Domestic spending remained resilient, productivity growth was strong, investment robust and job gains had kept pace with the workforce, while the unemployment rate had changed little. However, inflation continues to run above the Fedâs 2% target, leaving policymakers divided over whether monetary policy needs to tighten further. Governors Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissented from the decision, favouring a 25-basis-point rate hike. Their position reflects concerns that inflationary pressures remain persistent and that delaying further tightening could make it harder to bring price increases under control. Some economists and market participants have also suggested that another rate hike could come in December, although the Fed has not committed to a specific course. Warsh said the central bank needed more information to determine the appropriate policy stance, stressing that tackling inflation could not be tied to a fixed date or a single data point. He added that inflation expectations had moved in the right direction since the Fedâs September policy action, while financial and credit conditions had tightened for some businesses and households. However, he said he was unwilling to describe overall financial conditions as tight. Markets reacted cautiously to the decision. US stock indexes were mixed, Treasury yields edged higher and short-term interest rate futures rose, reflecting uncertainty over the path of monetary policy. The Fedâs statement leaves the possibility of further rate increases open if inflation fails to ease, even as policymakers acknowledge that employment and economic activity remain relatively strong. title: US arrests 2 dozen noncitizens in California over alleged illegal voter registration ahead of midterms
text: Federal authorities have arrested more than two dozen foreign nationals Monday in California. Federal authorities have arrested more than two dozen foreign nationals in California for allegedly registering and voting illegally in US elections, as the Trump administration intensifies its efforts to crack down on noncitizen voting ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. According to the Associated Press, the arrests were made on Monday as part of a statewide operation dubbed âOperation Protect the Voteâ. The Justice Department said all those arrested were lawful permanent residents, but not US citizens eligible to vote in federal elections. The accused face charges including making false statements on naturalisation applications and submitting fraudulent voter registrations. The crackdown comes despite data indicating that noncitizen voting is extremely rare in the US, difficult to establish and has not been shown to have changed the outcome of elections, AP reported. The arrests also mark a fresh escalation in the dispute between the Trump administration and California over voter registration records and election procedures. California at centre of voter roll dispute The Justice Department has made investigating noncitizen voting a priority this year, seeking detailed voter information from states, including dates of birth, addresses, driving licence numbers and partial Social Security numbers. Before Mondayâs arrests, federal prosecutors had charged around 90 people with various election-related offences this year, including about 50 accused of voting as noncitizens. The US had more than 227 million registered voters during the 2024 presidential election. California, a heavily Democratic state, has emerged as a major focus of the administrationâs efforts. Although it is not generally considered a key battleground in presidential elections, several competitive congressional races in the state could influence which party controls the US House of Representatives for the remaining two years of President Donald Trumpâs term. More than 23 million people are registered to vote in California. Last week, the Justice Department sued the state, seeking to prevent officials from counting mail-in ballots cast by people the federal government has identified as âlikelyâ noncitizens until their immigration status is verified. The lawsuit followed a dispute over a password-protected thumb drive containing a list of 20,000 names. Federal officials claimed the individuals were likely noncitizens who had been sent ballots for the November 3 election. California officials did not meet a 48-hour deadline set by the federal government to review the list. The state's secretary of state said the administration had provided no evidence to substantiate its claims, AP reported. California sends mail-in ballots to all registered voters. Justice Department warns election workers The dispute intensified on Friday when the Justice Department warned California election officials that knowingly processing or counting ballots cast by noncitizens could expose them to federal investigations and potential prosecution. In a letter addressed to the Los Angeles County Counselâs office, acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter said noncitizen voting in federal elections was a federal crime and warned that knowingly facilitating such conduct was also unlawful. The letter further cautioned that election workers who knowingly counted ballots cast by individuals identified by federal agencies as noncitizens could risk being treated as aiding and abetting a federal offence. The warning was also sent to California Secretary of State Shirley Weber and Los Angeles County Registrar Dean Logan, placing state and local election officials on notice less than three weeks before Election Day. Responding to the letter, Logan said his office remained focused on ensuring a fair and secure election, noting that Election Day was just 18 days away. He said the Justice Department had chosen to pursue its unverified claims through litigation and added that the matter was best addressed in court. You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. title: Speaker accepts resignations of Pathanmajra, Kunwar Vijay Partap; declares their seats vacant
text: Punjab assembly speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan Chandigarh: Punjab assembly speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan has accepted the resignations of former AAP MLAs Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Kunwar Vijay Partap Singh, and declared their assembly seats vacant with effect from Nov 2. Chetan Singh Jouramajra, who resigned from the AAP but not from the assembly, has been summoned by the Speaker for a hearing on Nov 5 after a representation by AAP chief whip Baljinder Kaur sought action against him under the anti-defection law. According to a notification issued by the Punjab assembly secretariat on Monday, Sanour MLA Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Amritsar North legislator Kunwar Vijay Partap Singh submitted their resignations on Nov 1. âKunwar Vijay Partap and Pathanmajra have resigned as per Article 190 (3) (b) of the Constitution on Nov 1,â read the notification. Their resignations were accepted by the speaker and seats were declared vacant with effect from Nov 2. In Jouramajraâs case, Sandhwan initiated proceedings after receiving a representation from Baljinder Kaur alleging that he had joined another political party. An official said the speaker issued a notice to Jouramajra, asking him to submit his response by Nov 5. Replying to a query, the speaker said he had summoned Jouramajra after receiving a representation from the AAP chief whip. He pointed out that the 10th Schedule of the Constitution provides for unseating an MLA if he quits the party on whose ticket he was elected. Earlier in the day, Kunwar Vijay Partap and Pathanmajra posted their resignations from the membership of Punjab Vidhan Sabha on Facebook. AAP leadership said all three functionaries had been suspended from the party over alleged anti-party activities. Kunwar Vijay Partap Singh was suspended from the AAP for five years in June last year for alleged anti-party activities. On Sunday, in a letter to Punjab AAP president Aman Arora, Kunwar Vijay Partap wrote, âThis is to bring to your kind notice that I have tendered my resignation as a member of the Punjab legislative assembly with effect from Nov 1, 2026. I hereby resign from all forms of the Aam Aadmi Party with immediate effect.â Punjab assemblyâs present term ends on March 16, 2027. As such, the Election Commission is unlikely to hold bypolls for these seats. Disqualification Plea Pending A disqualification petition against Banga MLA Sukhwinder Kumar Sukhi, who switched from the Shiromani Akali Dal to the Aam Aadmi Party in Aug 2024, is still pending before Punjab Vidhan Sabha speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan. The petition was filed by advocate H C Arora in Sept 2024, seeking Sukhiâs disqualification under the anti-defection law. The matter remains undecided. title: Rahul already suffered 56 losses before Gyanendra became CEC, says Patra
text: Sambit Patra in Kashi Varanasi: Escalating the BJP âs counterattack on Rahul Gandhi âs allegations against the Election Commission , party spokesperson Sambit Patra on Monday accused the Congress leader of misleading the nation with claims of the deletion of 13 crore votes. Citing the Congressâs record of repeated electoral defeats, Patra said the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls was a constitutional exercise aimed at updating voter lists, not the âvote theftâ being alleged by the opposition. A day after Gandhiâs mega show at Delhiâs Ramlila Maidan, Patra said the Congress has made it a habit to blame either EVMs or the EC after every electoral defeat. Patra said the BJP had won three Lok Sabha elections in 2014, 2019 and 2024 before Gyanendra Kumar became chief election commissioner on Feb 19, 2025. Referring to Rahulâs allegations against the Election Commission, he said the Congress lost 56 assembly elections between 2014 and 2025, and Rahul should explain those defeats instead of attacking constitutional institutions. He cited the 2014 Lok Sabha election, saying V S Sampath was the CEC then and had been appointed during Congress rule in 2012. âDid Congress appoint him to make Narendra Modi the Prime Minister?â Patra asked, adding that institutions should not be targeted for political convenience. Patra also said the Congress has been out of power for decades in several states, including Tamil Nadu for 59 years, West Bengal for 49 years, Uttar Pradesh for 37 years, Bihar for 36 years, Tripura for 33 years and Odisha for 26 years. He said these defeats were due to the Congressâs political failures, not voter-list revision. Defending the SIR, Patra said it had been conducted 12 times in the country, 10 times under Congress govts and twice under BJP govts. He said names are removed on four grounds, including absent, shifted, deceased and duplicate voters. Rahul Gandhi was combining different categories to falsely allege the theft of 13 crore votes, he added. He said around three crore people were marked absent, six crore applied through Form-6 for inclusion, and notices were issued to six crore shifted voters. Patra also said 2.37 crore young voters aged 18 to 28 had been added since June 2025. Targeting former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee, Patra said only Indian citizens have the right to vote and infiltrators cannot be allowed into voter lists. He challenged Congress and Samajwadi Party booth agents to identify errors instead of making allegations. title: BJP fields Puri from MP for Nov 12 Rajya Sabha bypolls
text: Hardeep Puri Bhopal: The BJP on Wednesday nominated Union petroleum minister Hardeep Singh Puri as its candidate for the Nov 12 Rajya Sabha by-election in Madhya Pradesh, choosing a leader from outside the state to fill the vacancy in the Upper House arising from the resignation of member L Murugan . The seat fell vacant after Murugan resigned his Rajya Sabha seat on Oct 13. His term was due to end in April 2030. He was elected to the Upper House from Madhya Pradesh in April 2024. The nomination puts to rest speculations around Puri, whose existing Rajya Sabha term from Uttar Pradesh is due to end on Nov 25, amid a rumoured upcoming Union cabinet reshuffle. His election from Madhya Pradesh would now enable him to continue as a member of the Upper House beyond that date. Madhya Pradesh has 11 Rajya Sabha seats. With Muruganâs resignation, 10 are occupied and one is vacant. The BJP is expected to retain the seat given its strength in the 230-member Madhya Pradesh assembly, where it has 164 MLAs against Congressâs 65. The Bharat Adivasi Party has one MLA. The Election Commission has scheduled polling and counting for Nov 12, with Nov 2 as the last date for filing nominations. Puri currently holds the petroleum and natural gas portfolio in the Union cabinet. Murugan, who had represented Madhya Pradesh in the Rajya Sabha, resigned to return to Tamil Nadu and focus on strengthening the BJP ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha election. title: Can you still vote today? When does early voting in midterms end in US?
text: A record number of early votes have been cast in the US midterm elections US midterm elections this time saw an unprecedented surge in early voting as more than 50.5 million early votes have been cast across the US as of Saturday morning. This is more than 5 million votes more than the number of early votes recorded in the 2022 midterm elections, an analysis by the University of Florida revealed. About 10.7 million registered Democrats have voted so far, according to the states that collate such information, compared with 7.8 million registered Republicans. In Texas's Harris County which includes Houston, 862,700 people had voted as of Wednesday, an Associated Press analysis found, compared with 564,500 at the same point in 2022. Can you vote today? Yes, though it will depend on your state and county as many states closed early voting. When did early voting begin? Early voting began as early as September 18. September 18: Minnesota, South Dakota, Virginia September 19: Vermont September 24: Illinois October 5: California, Maine, Montana, Nebraska October 6: Indiana, New Mexico, Ohio October 7: Arizona October 13: Georgia, Idaho October 14: Iowa, Kansas, Rhode Island, Tennessee October 15: North Carolina October 16: Washington October 17: Massachusetts, Nevada October 19: Alaska, Arkansas, Colorado, South Carolina, Texas October 20: Hawaii, Louisiana, Missouri, Utah October 21: West Virginia October 22: Delaware, Maryland October 24: Florida, Michigan, New Jersey, New York October 26: Washington DC October 28: Oklahoma October 29: Kentucky When did early voting close? In many states, early voting closed by October 31. In some states, early voting will continue until the Election Day on November 3. October 30: Arizona, Georgia, Idaho, Massachusetts, Nevada, Texas, Utah October 31: Florida, Kentucky, New Mexico, North Carolina, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Virginia, West Virginia November 1: Connecticut, Delaware, Michigan, New Jersey, New York, Ohio (Cuyahoga County), Wisconsin November 2: Arkansas, Illinois, Indiana, Minnesota, Montana, Nebraska, Rhode Island, Vermont, Wyoming November 3 (Election Day): Alaska, Colorado, Hawaii, Washington. Can US voters cast their vote online? No, there is no online voting. The three ways to cast votes are: In-person voting: At polling stations, using paper ballots or voting machines. Mail-in/absentee voting: Eligible voters can receive and return ballots by mail or designated drop boxes. Overseas US voters: US citizens living abroad, including in India, can request ballots electronically. title: Brazil stalls momentum of Donroe Doctrine
text: - As it became clear that the incumbent President Luiz InÃ¡cio Lula da Silva of Brazil defeated his challenger FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro by 51.79%-48.21% margin in the presidential runoff on October 25, a result that was not to the liking of Donald J Trump, the US President returned to his familiar theme of vote rigging. âI didn't take sides,â the US President said, before adding that the election âlooked like another rigged electionâ. Never before in Brazilâs democratic history had a presidential candidate lost the first round and gone on to win the runoff. Despite losing the October 25 election by 4.4 million votes, Flavio Bolsonaro has not conceded and has called for the election to be annulled. He has left Brazil soon after the loss after being ordered to surrender his passports following federal investigations against him. Trump may not have explicitly endorsed Flavio Bolsonaro during the election campaign, but he made no secret of whom he wanted to win, either. Just three weeks earlier, on October 4, when Lula da Silva lost the first round of the polls to Bolsonaro by more than 3 per cent of the vote, the US President called it a âvery bigâ victory. Flavio Bolsonaro's father Jair Bolsonaro was nicknamed 'Trump of the Tropics' when he governed Brazil between 2019 and 2022. Last year, when Jair Bolsonaro stood on trial in the country's Supreme Federal Court on charges of leading a conspiracy to mount a military coup to deprive Lula da Silva of the presidency that he won over him in the 2021 election, Trump termed it "witch hunt" in a social media post. He compared the prosecution to the legal cases he himself faced between his two presidential terms. "This is nothing more, or less, than an attack on a Political Opponent - Something I know much about! It happened to me, times 10," Trump said. He praised Jair Bolsonaro as a "strong leader" who "truly loved his country". Jair Bolsonaro was convicted by the Supreme Federal Court in November 2025 and sentenced to more than 27 years in prison for conspiring an armed insurrection against the state. US-Brazil ties nose-dived since last year largely due to Trumpâs vehement opposition to Jair Bolsonaro's prosecution, with Washington imposing punitive tariffs on Brazil as a political response to the trial. Trumpâs relations with Lula da Silva also hit a rock-bottom as a result. What also rankled the US President with Lula da Silvaâs re-election was the stalling of Latin Americaâs right-wing swing. It had swung to the right since Trump ally Javier Milei's election victory in Argentina in 2023. Ecuador, Chile, Colombia and Peru have all elected presidents who are closely aligned with the Trump administrationâs worldview since then. Venezuela also has a pro-US government after the US military intervention in January this year. The month after the US intervention in Venezuela, in the State of the Union address this year, President Trump vowed never to relinquish American dominance in the Western Hemisphere, a strategy he has dubbed the âDonroe Doctrineâ, in a nod to the early 19 th century Monroe Doctrine. Therefore, it is not hard to understand why a âvery bigâ victory in the first round turned out to be âanother rigged electionâ in Brazil for the US President when the candidate he favoured lost. title: Rare White House visit by top US commander puts Trump's Iran strike options in focus
text: Adm. Brad Cooper and US president Trump The top US military commander in the Middle East held a rare in-person briefing with US president Donald Trump on Thursday to discuss the state of the Iran war, including the effectiveness of Washingtonâs naval blockade and military options for a possible resumption of major combat operations, according to reports by The Wall Street Journal and Axios. Admiral Brad Cooper, head of US Central Command (CENTCOM), met Trump at the White House alongside defence secretary Pete Hegseth, joint chiefs chairman General Dan Caine and other senior officials. Treasury secretary Scott Bessent and White House envoy Steve Witkoff also attended, Axios reported, citing two US officials. Cooper briefed Trump on whether the naval blockade was achieving its objectives, the operation to guide oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz towards global energy markets, and the economic pressure campaign being conducted by the military in coordination with the Treasury Department, according to Axios. WSJ separately reported that the meeting covered military options for Iran and came as Washington weighs resuming major combat operations. The rare in-person briefing comes as Trump pursues two tracks: trying to revive negotiations with Tehran while preparing for the possibility of renewed strikes after the US midterm elections. WSJ has reported that US officials have told Arab Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense campaign after the elections. Trump hinted at the possibility of renewed military action last week. âWe may do another little Epic Fury,â he said at a rally, referring to the US-Israeli bombing campaign in the spring. âOr theyâll agree.â Diplomacy continues amid military preparations Regional mediators led by Qatar are trying to prevent a resumption of hostilities after the midterms and steer Washington and Tehran back towards negotiations. âThe mediation is at a very sensitive stage,â a regional source told Axios. Qatari mediators recently delivered a letter from vice-president JD Vance to Iranâs Supreme National Security Council secretary, Mohsen Rezaei, proposing a restart of negotiations while stressing that any talks would have to address Iranâs nuclear programme, Axios reported. The Journal has also reported that Vance engaged the Iranian hard-liner in an effort to revive peace negotiations. Trump and Vance met on Wednesday to discuss a possible gesture of goodwill towards Iran, such as sending humanitarian supplies, including food and medicine, according to a source cited by Axios. Trump later publicly backed the idea. He has denied directing Vance to initiate peace talks, saying the contact concerned medical supplies. US Ambassador to Turkey Tom Barrack said Thursday that Washington and Tehran were âvery closeâ to an agreement to de-escalate tensions. âI think weâre very close to finally getting to a place where we can say, âLetâs just have a timeout,ââ Barrack told CNN, while cautioning that a comprehensive solution would not come immediately. Iran, however, has continued to demand that Washington lift the blockade, release frozen Iranian funds and allow Tehran to sell oil before nuclear negotiations resume. Pentagon strengthens regional defences The Pentagon has laid the groundwork for a possible renewed bombing campaign in recent weeks, deploying additional air defences, munitions and supplies to the Middle East and moving some troops away from bases considered vulnerable to Iranian retaliation. The US Army is also moving an additional Patriot air-defence battery to Israel amid concerns about a shortage of missile interceptors and efforts to replenish supplies. Iran has threatened to strike a broad range of US and Gulf targets in response to any American attack. Tehran has also resumed producing ballistic missiles using stockpiled components in underground facilities and stepped up efforts to target US personnel in the region. The prospect of renewed hostilities has alarmed some US lawmakers. title: US finds Chinese spy in Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's circle; China calls it a smear; Nvidia says: Jensen talks with thousands of...
text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang American intelligence agencies have concluded that a Chinese businesswoman with a close relationship to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was passing information to Beijing, according to a New York Times report. The woman, Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, is a Chinese citizen and a top executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre company already under US scrutiny for allegedly steering advanced Nvidia AI chips to China. President Donald Trump was briefed on the findings about a year ago and chose not to act, the report says. Jensen Huang has not received a defensive briefing, the warning US agencies sometimes give Americans targeted by foreign spies. Surveillance of Alice Huang is still ongoing, and companies linked to her kept buying Nvidia chips this year. China has rejected the allegation. Liu Chang, spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy in Washington, accused the US of running a campaign of baseless smears against Beijing. Nvidia played it down. Spokesperson John Rizzo said Huang's meetings with her were neither unusual nor unexpected, adding that "Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year." He said customers like Megaspeed get routine business information, not trade secrets, and nothing relevant to national security. Megaspeed said it has hired outside counsel for an internal probe and will cooperate with the US government. US surveillance of a Megaspeed executive led officials straight to Jensen Huang Citing people briefed on the matter, NYT reports that US agencies were electronically monitoring Alice Huang when they found she was in contact with an American citizen. A process known as unmasking later identified that person as the Nvidia chief. When Trump was first briefed, officials did not think Jensen Huang knew what she was doing. Some senior administration officials now doubt he could have stayed in the dark. The two were photographed at a Taipei bar in June 2024, sharing whiskey with other AI executives after a trade show. They were spotted again leaving a business dinner in the city in May 2025. Megaspeed bought $4.8 billion of Nvidia-powered gear in under two years Megaspeed's Malaysian sister company bought at least $4.8 billion worth of advanced AI equipment with Nvidia chips between June 2024 and February 2026, NYT reports, citing ImportGenius trade records. The firm buys chips, builds data centres in Southeast Asia and rents the computing power to Chinese companies, with Alibaba as its main client. US investigators suspect some of those chips are slipping into China illegally. The Commerce Department began looking into Megaspeed in late 2024, after an official visiting its Malaysian data centre found the Nvidia equipment still sitting in boxes. That case has since moved to the Justice Department. The findings surface weeks before Trump's visit to China next month, where chip exports are likely to be on the agenda. Jensen Huang has spent Trump's second term lobbying to ease curbs on Nvidia sales to China, and he sat at the head table when Xi Jinping attended a White House state dinner last month. title: One battle after another?
text: After the US midterms, Trump faces a choice on restarting the Iran war â one that could push oil past $140 a barrel and hit India's growth, rupee and markets hard. Last month, Trump promised that he would not attack Iran before the US midterm elections. So far, he has kept his promise. But what will he do once the elections are over? Nobody knows. Betting markets, where people put money on what they think will happen, offer some clues. On Monday evening, Polymarket showed a 94% chance that the ceasefire would continue until Wednesday. But by Sunday, this had fallen to 76%. Could Trump really attack Iran again? Once the elections are over, there may be little to stop him. He still has three aircraft carriers in the Arabian Sea, and he may want to show that the US has not backed down. But this could create serious trouble for everyone. Iran is unlikely to stay silent if it is attacked. Mojtaba Khamenei has warned that Iran's response will not be limited to any particular region. This could mean fresh attacks on oil and gas facilities across West Asia. In the worst case, experts believe oil prices could cross $140 a barrel and remain high. Winter is beginning, and Europe and America need more oil to heat homes. Their stored supplies have also fallen. For India, such high oil prices would mean costlier goods, higher interest rates, less foreign exchange to fall back on, a weaker rupee and falling share prices. It would also become harder for India to maintain 7% economic growth. But another war is not certain. On Monday morning, oil prices fell after Iran held talks with Qatari officials, who are trying to help end the war. At his Halloween party, Trump also left the door open to peace. When reporters asked about the war, he said that talks were going well. Another factor is the US Congress. Democrats may gain control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. They cannot directly stop Trump from starting a war, but they can make it harder for him by limiting the money available for it. Betting markets put the Democrats' chances of winning control of the House very high. They also give the party a 73% chance of taking control of the Senate. Trump may not worry much about the financial pain ordinary people face. But he cares about his public image and often boasts about the strength of the US economy under his leadership. Democrats have blamed the rise in prices on the Iran war. Will Trump want to be blamed for expensive heating bills this winter? US share prices have risen sharply, helped by excitement over AI. But a rise in energy costs could hurt the market. In 2022, after Russia invaded Ukraine, high inflation and rising interest rates ended a big rise in cryptocurrency prices. A similar shock from the Iran war could hurt the AI boom and slow down the US economy. Trump may not want these problems to become part of his record. We can only hope he chooses not to restart the war. Disclaimer : Views expressed above are the author's own.

title: AAP discusses Punjab poll candidates at Kejriwalâs residence; first list due October 31
text: Discussions were led by national convenor Arvind Kejriwal and Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Singh Mann CHANDIGARH: The Aam Aadmi Party 's (AAP) Political Affairs Committee (PAC), the party's top decision-making body, met at the residence of national convenor Arvind Kejriwal on Friday to discuss candidates for the upcoming Punjab assembly elections . Kejriwal, Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Singh Mann, party Punjab in-charge Manish Sisodia, AAP leader Satyendar Jain and Jasmine Shah attended the meeting, news agency ANI reported. Punjab finance minister Harpal Cheema and state AAP president Aman Arora joined the deliberations through video conferencing. After the meeting, Mann said the names of assembly candidates had been discussed and that the process would continue at the next PAC meeting. "The names of assembly candidates were discussed today," Mann said. "The names will be discussed again during the PAC meeting tomorrow, October 31. The first list of candidates will be released tomorrow," he added, ANI reported. On Wednesday, a delegation of the Election Commission of India (ECI) conducted a district-wise review of poll preparedness for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. The delegation comprised senior deputy election commissioner Pawan Kumar Sharma, deputy election commissioner Bhanu Prakash Yeturu, director general (IT) Seema Khanna and director general (Media) Ashish Goyal. During the meeting, the delegation interacted with all 23 district election officers, commissioners of police and senior superintendents of police. Officials gave presentations on the status of election preparedness in their respective districts, ANI reported. The visiting officials emphasised strict compliance with ECI guidelines, transparency in administrative processes, timely execution of pre-poll activities and robust enforcement measures across the state. The chief electoral officer of Punjab assured the delegation that all election-related tasks would be carried out diligently and within the stipulated timelines, in accordance with the Election Commission's instructions, to ensure free, fair, transparent and inclusive polls. Meanwhile, Hardev Singh Ubha, a senior Punjab BJP leader, met Harjit Singh Grewal, chairman of the National Commission for Minorities, at the Commission's office in New Delhi and raised several public issues concerning Punjab and Mohali, ANI reported. During the meeting, Ubha highlighted concerns over drug abuse and the alleged death of a young man in Mansa, recurring fires at the Phase 5 dumping ground in Mohali, lack of canal water supply in several residential areas and villages, compensation for farmers affected by land acquisition in Sector 87, and delays in constructing a bridge connecting Sectors 66/67 with Sectors 80/81. He requested that the issues be brought to the attention of the concerned authorities for appropriate intervention and timely resolution in the public interest. Ubha also raised the death of Daljit Singh alias Jeeta, son of Sardar Jarnail Singh and a resident of Bhamme Kalan village in Mansa district, allegedly due to a drug overdose. title: Was just âcuriousâ and left when cops asked: Imran Khan in plea
text: Bombay High Court has adjourned the hearing on Imran Khan Pal's challenge to a notice until November 2 MUMBAI: Bombay High Court on Tuesday posted to Nov 2 the hearing on actor Imran Khan Palâs challenge to a notice directing him to leave India and till then kept the notice in abeyance. The Oct 28 deadline under the Oct 14 notice issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) under the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, was extended till the next hearing after Additional Solicitor General Anil Singh appearing for the Centre sought a short adjournment. Khan, born in the US, has been in India for almost 42 years since the age of two years. He holds an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) status under the Citizenship Act, 1955. The HC bench of Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna recorded in the brief order that senior counsel V R Dhond appearing for the actor had âfairlyâ not opposed such a request for adjournment. Khanâs plea says power to remove a person under Section 29 of the Foreigners Act was intended to safeguard national sovereignty and security, and could not be used to punish a public figure merely for being present near a protest site or expressing concern over restrictions on the movement of people in the city. His expulsion could undermine confidence of the US-based Indian diaspora in the OCI regime and raise concerns for the US, whose citizen he is. On Tuesday, lawyer Sunil Kumar, represented by advocate Subhash Jha, intervened in the matter, contending that the FRRO notice falls under criminal jurisdiction and that Khanâs civil petition could thus not be heard. Khanâs senior counsel, V R Dhond, questioned the intervenerâs locus to raise the objection. The matter was kept back for Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to appear online for the FRRO, a central govt authority, from New Delhi. However, ASG Anil Singh later sought an adjournment to enable the solicitor general to appear, following which the court posted the matter to Nov 2. The notice followed an FIR registered against him for allegedly participating in a protest in Mumbai on Oct 10 in support of the Cockroach Janata Partyâs (CJP) agitation against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi. Khanâs plea said he was merely âcuriousâ when he was passing by and saw the crowd and had left immediately when the police asked him to. Khan (around 44), also represented by lawyers Zulfiquar Memon, Parvez Memon and Kunal Vajani, contended that the notice was arbitrary, disproportionate and issued without hearing him, thus flouting his fundamental rights to equality and life under Articles 14 and 21, which apply to non-Indian citizens as well. Arguing that the notice imposed the ultimate consequence on the basis of a mere allegation, the petition said the authorities could not proceed with his expulsion without allowing the criminal justice process to take its course. title: Modi, Shah to spearhead BJPâs campaign for UP polls
text: Union home minister Amit Shah Prime Minister Narendra Modi Union home minister Amit Shah Prime Minister Narendra Modi Union home minister Amit Shah 1 2 Lucknow: BJP is preparing to shift its UP campaign into high gear, with PM Narendra Modi , Union home minister Amit Shah and party national president Nitin Nabin set to spearhead a series of high-profile engagements over a period of one month, signalling the beginning of partyâs intensified organisational and political combat ahead of 2027 elections. The first signs of this mobilisation will be visible on Sunday, when Modi visits his constituency Varanasi to attend the concluding display of the Indian Air Forceâs air show, Wings Over Ganga, at NaMo Ghat. The PM is also scheduled to visit Mirzamurad to inaugurate a new industrial unit of Arvind Mills, projected to generate around 1,000 direct jobs. Watch PM Modi Watches IAF Air Show In Varanasi, Inaugurates Garment Unit Amid Border Row Although no political rally is on Modiâs itinerary, BJP is expected to make the most of his visit to showcase its political strength in his parliamentary constituency. The high-profile engagements come as the party begins groundwork for a state-wide campaign, with organisational consolidation and the revival of its electoral machinery emerging as immediate priorities. From Varanasi, the spotlight is expected to shift to BJPâs much-awaited state executive meeting, where Amit Shah is likely to take stock of the organisation and outline partyâs roadmap for 2027 state polls. Party sources said Shahâs proposed participation in the meeting assumes particular significance even as the BJP seeks to recalibrate its strategy after its unexpected poor performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections in UP against the Samajwadi Party. The party has since been reviewing its electoral setbacks, examining district- and constituency-level performance and identifying organisational gaps that may have cost it crucial seats. Shah, widely credited with orchestrating the BJPâs sweeping victory in the 2017 UP elections, is expected to push for a high-intensity, micro-targeted campaign that combines booth-level mobilisation with sharper social and caste outreach. The challenge before the BJP is to recover lost ground while countering an emboldened opposition led by the SP and its ally Congress. The partyâs next phase of preparations is therefore expected to focus not merely on energising its cadre but also on tightening coordination between its organisational leadership, govt and alliance partners. With Modi and Shah expected to anchor the initial phase of the campaign, BJP is also preparing to put the strength of the National Democratic Alliance on public display. A key event in this strategy is a proposed joint rally with ally Om Prakash Rajbharâs Suheldev Bhartiya Samaj Party (SBSP) in Azamgarh on Nov 29. Tentatively billed as the Samajik Samrasta Maharally, the event is expected to be attended by Nitin Nabin, Yogi Adityanath and UP BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary. Other NDA partners, including Apna Dal (S), the Nishad Party and the Rashtriya Lok Dal, are also expected to participate. SBSP national general secretary Arun Rajbhar confirmed that the rally would be a âshow of strengthâ by the BJP-led NDA in eastern Uttar Pradesh or Purvanchal. The choice of Azamgarh is politically significant. Regarded as an SP bastion, the district presents the BJP-led alliance with an opportunity to challenge the opposition on its home turf and demonstrate that its social coalition remains intact ahead of the Assembly polls. In the 2022 Assembly elections, SP won all 10 seats in Azamgarh district. The party subsequently won the Azamgarh Lok Sabha seat in 2024 Lok Sabha elections with SPâs Dharmendra Yadav defeating BJP candidate Dinesh Lal Yadav âNirahuaâ by more than 1.6 lakh votes. The proposed rally is thus being positioned as more than a show of alliance unity. It is also expected to serve as a platform for consolidating the BJPâs outreach among OBCs, particularly the Most Backward Classes (MBCs), whose electoral support could prove crucial in the closely contested political battle ahead.
